title: A login profile that writes to stdout is spliced into resolved dotfile content
description:
Provider-sourced dotfile content is the command's ENTIRE stdout. When that command runs under a login shell, the login profile's own stdout is captured into the same stream and becomes part of the deployed file.

Mechanism, verified:
- ShellCommandRunner::login_shell (commands/shell.rs:77-92) sets login: true; build_command (:98-102) adds '-l', so the shell sources the user's login profile.
- run_capture (dotfile_service/resolve.rs) returns output.stdout() as the resolved content, byte for byte. Nothing separates profile output from command output -- they are the same fd.
- So a .zprofile / .bash_profile / config.fish containing an echo, a banner, a version-manager notice, or a 'motd'-style greeting produces content like 'banner\n<secret>' written into the target.

Why this matters more than a cosmetic corruption: the target is frequently a credentials file. A ~/.netrc, an ~/.aws/credentials, a token file with a leading banner line is silently malformed. The failure is quiet -- the deploy reports success, the file exists, and the breakage shows up later in whatever consumes it.

Existing gates do NOT catch it: the empty check (resolve.rs:175-179) passes because the content is non-empty, and MAX_CONTENT_BYTES (:180-182) passes because a banner makes it larger, not smaller, and only by a few bytes. There is no format validation -- by design, since selfie does not know what the target's format is.

ALREADY LIVE, not hypothetical: the MCP server has run provider commands under login_shell since 31bf6bc (mcp-server/src/server.rs:228), and install/check/audit have since 9e918a7. selfie-w8gd (U3) will extend it to CLI apply, which is where the bytes actually land in a credentials file -- so the exposure grows, but it is pre-existing and NOT introduced by that unit.

Nothing in the code or docs warns about it. docs/package-files.md says only that provider commands 'run through a shell'.

Fix directions, none obviously right:
- run the login shell so profile stdout is discarded and only the command's own output is captured (hard -- there is no clean fd separation through 'sh -l -c')
- warn when resolved provider content changes after a no-op command, or when a control run of ':' produces non-empty stdout -- a cheap heuristic that catches the common case
- document it as a sharp edge and tell users to keep profiles silent, which is the weakest option but honest

Found by the selfie-w8gd/selfie-fbwo plan author (U3 of the command-execution batch); mechanism verified independently by the lead against shell.rs and resolve.rs.
notes:
CORRECTIONS TO THE DESCRIPTION ABOVE, from the U3 plan reviewer, each verified independently by the lead. RAISED TO P1.

1. PROVENANCE WAS WRONG. The description says the MCP server has run provider commands under login_shell 'since 31bf6bc'. It has not. git show 31bf6bc (2026-03-17, 'Use login shell in MCP server for full user PATH') touches only crates/mcp-server/src/main.rs and crates/selfie/src/commands/shell.rs -- it gave the PACKAGE service a login shell. The DOTFILE service's login-shell runner in crates/mcp-server/src/server.rs came from f888761 (2026-07-27), 'feat(dotfiles): resolve secret-bearing content at apply time'. Verified with git log -S login_shell -- crates/mcp-server/src/server.rs.

So this is three days old, not four months. Still pre-existing, still not introduced by selfie-w8gd -- but 'long-standing and unremarked' was the wrong framing.

2. BLAST RADIUS WAS OVERSTATED. The description says the hazard is live on 'install/check/audit'. It is not. resolve_content has exactly ONE production caller -- SecretApply::resolve at dotfile_service/service.rs:719 (the only other hit is a test at resolve.rs:463). Dotfile apply is the sole path where a command's stdout becomes FILE CONTENT. install/check/audit do run a login shell, but their stdout goes to status and events, never into a credentials file.

Corrected scope: exposed on exactly ONE surface today -- the MCP tool selfie_apply_dotfiles. selfie-w8gd adds a second: CLI 'selfie apply'.

3. RAISED P2 -> P1. Fewer surfaces than first filed, but the reviewer's argument holds: this silently corrupts credential files, the deploy reports success, and no gate catches it. A quiet wrong-bytes-on-disk defect on the credential path outranks a loud failure.

4. ONE ASYMMETRY WORTH KNOWING, and it points at the fix. The Template/vars path DOES have a partial detector -- a binding value containing a newline emits 'dotfile var X contains a line break; it will be substituted as-is'. The whole-file Provider path, which is exactly where a spliced banner lands, has no equivalent. Filed separately.

NOT A REASON TO BLOCK selfie-w8gd. Same defect, correct fix, and the mitigation has to be made for the MCP path regardless. That unit is required to disclose it in docs/package-files.md instead.
close_reason: Closed

title: run_buffered discards pipe read errors and returns a partial buffer as complete
description:
crates/selfie/src/commands/shell.rs:154 and :161 read a command's stdout and stderr with 'let _ = read_to_end(&mut out, &mut buf).await;'. An IO error part-way through the read is discarded and whatever was buffered so far is returned as if it were the command's complete output.

Consequences differ by path and the check path is the worst:
- check: a truncated stdout can flip a check result. A command whose output would have said 'installed' can be read as not installed, or the reverse, with no error surfaced.
- dotfile resolve: MAX_CONTENT_BYTES is checked against the truncated buffer, so a partial credential can pass the size cap and be written to the target. Same shape as the truncation hazard identified while evaluating selfie-mxo.
- audit and install: a partial log, reported as the whole.

Nothing distinguishes 'the command produced this' from 'the pipe failed and this is what we got'. run_buffered is the primitive behind execute, execute_with_timeout and execute_in_dir, so every non-streaming command path inherits it.

Fix: propagate the read error rather than discarding it. Note both reads happen in detached tokio tasks specifically to avoid the ~64KB pipe-buffer deadlock, so the error has to be carried back across the join rather than returned directly.

Found while planning selfie-mxo.
acceptance_criteria: A pipe read error surfaces as a command failure rather than a silently truncated buffer.
notes:
SEVERITY RAISED TO P1 after the selfie-mxo plan review enumerated the consumers. The bead as filed described a truncated buffer returned as complete. The four production consumers of that buffer make it worse than that framing:

1. crates/selfie/src/package/service/install.rs:268-269 uses stdout_str().trim() as an EXECUTABLE PATH. A partial read yields a truncated path — which either fails, or resolves to a DIFFERENT binary than the command reported. That is the worst of the four and was not in the original filing.
2. crates/selfie/src/dotfile_service/resolve.rs:268 is the only production consumer of raw stdout(). A partial read writes a TRUNCATED CREDENTIAL to the target: bytes.len() > MAX_CONTENT_BYTES is then false, so the size cap at resolve.rs:181 — the only gate — does not fire. Verified by the reviewer against the code.
3. check.rs:261/271 — a truncated stdout can flip a check result.
4. audit.rs:266 — a partial source list reported as complete.

Exact sites: crates/selfie/src/commands/shell.rs:157 and :164, both 'let _ = tokio::io::AsyncReadExt::read_to_end(&mut out, &mut buf).await;'. (Earlier note said 154/161; corrected against the tree.)

Note this is the SAME hazard that made selfie-mxo's proposed fix dangerous: pre-emptive truncation would defeat the post-hoc size cap on the credential path. mxo concluded truncation must never be introduced for that reason — and this bead is that failure already reachable without it.

Fix: propagate the read error rather than discarding it. Both reads happen in detached tokio tasks to avoid the ~64KB pipe-buffer deadlock, so the error must be carried back across the join rather than returned directly.
close_reason: Closed

title: dotfiles track accepts a symlinked target silently, deferring the refusal to a later apply
description:
After selfie-4m9, 'selfie apply' REFUSES to deploy to a symlinked target. But 'selfie dotfiles track' still accepts one without comment and records it as tracked.

The user therefore learns nothing at the moment they could act cheaply — when they are standing at the target, know why the symlink is there, and could 'rm' it in seconds — and instead gets a refusal at the next apply, possibly weeks later, with the context gone.

Verified by probe during selfie-4m9 implementation.

track already knows the target path and can stat it. It should say at track time that the target is a symlink and that apply will refuse it, ideally naming the destination. Whether it should refuse to track outright, or track with a warning, is the substance of this issue: refusing is more consistent, warning is friendlier if the user intends to remove the link before applying.

Related: selfie-paa5 would add an opt-in to follow symlinks, which changes what track should say.
acceptance_criteria: Tracking a symlinked target tells the user at track time that apply will refuse it.
notes:
RAISED P2 -> P1 (2026-07-31). Track does more than fail to warn: it silently copies the SYMLINK DESTINATION's content into the dotfiles repository, which sync push commits to a git remote. Chain verified independently, link by link, by the unit's plan author and again by its reviewer:

1. Track reads THROUGH the link. handle_track_standalone (service.rs:1626) and handle_track_for_package (service.rs:1755) both call filesystem.read_file(&expanded_target); RealFileSystem::read_file (fs/real.rs:33) is fs::read_to_string, which follows symlinks.
2. It copies the destination's content into the repo. Measured: target config.toml -> symlink -> real_secrets containing DESTINATION_CONTENT_TOKEN=abc123; after track, dotfiles/myapp/config.toml holds that content. Same for track_for_package.
3. Silently. Success(DotfileTracked{was_already_tracked:false}), ZERO warnings, both handlers.
4. It writes a spec -- dotfiles/myapp.yml, plain source/target entry.
5. It records deploy state for a deploy THAT NEVER HAPPENED: source_checksum == deployed_checksum == checksum of the link destination, with a deployed_at timestamp. The target is still a symlink; nothing was ever written to it.
6. sync push commits it. push discovers the repo by walking up from package_directory (sync_service/service.rs:284-287). track_for_package writes inside that repo unconditionally and is grouped by infer_package_name (service.rs:816-834), so no --include-ungrouped is needed. track_standalone writes into dotfiles_directory, which docs/sync.md:139 makes MANDATORY to be in the same repository.

So: another tool symlinks a credential-adjacent file into place (stow, yadm, Syncthing), the user tracks it, and its contents are copied into a repo that gets pushed. No warning at any step.

IT ALSO MANUFACTURES selfie-qvwq. The full timeline was reproduced: track (silent) -> drift reports drift_count=0 'in sync' -> apply silently skips -> user edits the repo file -> 'repo changed' FOREVER, apply refusing every round. The entire failure timeline in qvwq is created by the one track that said nothing.

DECIDED: REFUSE, not warn. The deciding argument, from the reviewer: there is NO configuration in which a tracked symlinked target does what the user asked. It is either permanently inert (destination content matches, nothing ever happens) or permanently broken (the moment the repo file is edited, apply refuses forever). Refusing removes an option that never worked. A warning cannot repair it either -- all three side effects are wrong independently, and there is no correct answer to 'which content' for a target that can never be deployed.

Also fixed by placing the refusal before the existence check: track on a DANGLING symlink today fails with 'Target file does not exist', which is misleading -- the named path does exist, it is a link, and path_exists follows.

Being fixed now as unit A of the target-semantics batch, alongside selfie-qvwq and selfie-86o.
close_reason: Closed

title: deny_unknown_fields on DotfileEntry reintroduces the YAML anchor bug 826e854 fixed
description:
Commit 826e854 ('fix: allow YAML anchors while still catching unknown fields') removed #[serde(deny_unknown_fields)] from Package, EnvironmentConfig and DotfileEntry, replacing detection with a flatten-into-HashMap plus a validation pass that permits underscore-prefixed anchor keys and reports anything else as a field-level error. Provider-sourced dotfiles re-added the attribute to DotfileEntry to catch a 'var:' for 'vars:' typo, which reintroduces the bug that commit fixed.

Verified empirically against the merged tree:
  _anchor: &a hello  inside a dotfiles entry  ->  REJECTED, 'unknown field _anchor'
That is the exact '_brew: &brew' case named in 826e854's message.

Second consequence: a typo inside a dotfiles entry now fails the WHOLE package file to parse, so it drops out of valid_packages, taking that package's other dotfiles and all its install and check commands with it. The user gets 'skipping unparsable package file' rather than a field-level diagnostic naming the key, and none of the package's other issues are checked.

The typo-catching goal is right and the regression test for it should stay. The mechanism is the one already tried and deliberately backed out. Fix by extending the existing flatten-plus-validate mechanism down to DotfileEntry rather than by the attribute, so anchors keep working and a typo produces a field-level error.
acceptance_criteria: A YAML anchor inside a dotfiles entry parses; a misspelled key produces a field-level validation error rather than failing the whole file.
close_reason:
Fixed in PR #71 (merged 6786b48). deny_unknown_fields replaced with a hand-written Deserialize for DotfileEntry that records unrecognized keys into unknown_keys and skips _-prefixed ones, so YAML anchors parse again and a misspelled key produces a field-level error instead of failing the whole package file. content_source() returns the existing ContentSource::Invalid so apply refuses the entry — fail-closed.

Two fail-open paths were found by review and closed in the same PR:
1. Removing deny_unknown_fields alone made apply report Success/deployed_count:1 while writing an unrendered '{{ api_key }}' over a credentials target. Found at the plan gate.
2. save_package re-serializes from the struct, so any load-mutate-save silently deleted the offending key and the NEXT apply deployed the credentials file. Guard placed inside save_package rather than at its callers — there are five production call sites, two of which (spec create, standalone dotfiles track) were on nobody's list. Found at final review.

serde(flatten) was deliberately avoided: it forecloses Spanned<T> on these fields, which d96b82c had to back out of Package for, and would block selfie-2wb.

Residual documented and tracked: selfie-kj5y (a _-prefixed key shadowing a real field, e.g. _vars:, deploys unrendered with no diagnostic).

title: Dotfile deploys write through symlinked targets
description:
expand_user_path (crates/selfie/src/dotfile_service/service.rs:226) calls FileSystem::expand_path, which canonicalizes (crates/selfie/src/fs/real.rs:43). Canonicalization resolves symlinks, so perform_deploy receives a symlink-resolved target and writes through any symlink at the target path, silently overwriting the link's destination rather than replacing the link.

Security-relevant on its own: a symlink planted at a dotfile target redirects written content to a path the planter chose. It also nullifies the symlink protection of write_file_private for any caller that canonicalizes first, which constrains how secret-bearing dotfiles must resolve their target.

Deciding the right behavior is the work here: replacing a symlinked target is a behavior change for users who deliberately symlink their dotfiles, so this is not simply 'stop canonicalizing'.
acceptance_criteria: Deploy either refuses to write through a symlinked target or does so only by explicit opt-in; behavior is documented and tested.
notes:
Provider-sourced dotfiles (selfie-doh) deliberately does NOT route secret targets through expand_user_path. It uses its own expand_secret_target, which expands ~ and normalizes . and .. but never canonicalizes, so the final path component reaches write_file_private unresolved and its symlink guarantee actually holds for credential writes.

That divergence is intentional and load-bearing, not an oversight. Whoever fixes this issue must UNIFY the two expansions by bringing the repo-file path up to the secret path's behavior — not by deleting the secret path's expansion in the name of removing duplication, which would silently reintroduce the vulnerability for credentials.
close_reason:
Fixed in PR #72 (merged 78ae893). Deploy now REFUSES a symlinked target via libc::O_NOFOLLOW rather than writing through it; the link and its destination are left untouched, a warning names both paths, and the entry is counted as skipped.

The bead's diagnosis was incomplete. Canonicalization in expand_user_path was half of it — fs::write follows a final-component symlink regardless — but fixing only the write leaves the main case broken, because the expansion hands the write site an already-resolved destination. Measured: each half alone produces IDENTICAL wrong behavior (destination overwritten, counted as deployed, no warning), which is why neither can be dropped as cleanup.

Three layers: expand_target_path no longer canonicalizes (the former expand_secret_target, body unchanged — the repository path was brought UP to the credential path's behavior, never the reverse); a check hoisted into handle_apply so dry-run does not preview a refused deploy and the conflict resolver is never asked an unanswerable question; and O_NOFOLLOW at the write as the only TOCTOU protection, pinned by the_writer_refuses_even_when_the_check_is_blinded (a decorator test with an AtomicUsize control).

REPLACE-the-symlink was considered and rejected: measured, it destroys a deliberate symlink on the unprompted RepoChanged path on the first ordinary apply after any repo edit. Opt-in to follow symlinks deliberately is selfie-paa5.

Ten attacks verified refused including the dangling-link case the bead predicted was already safe; TOCTOU confirmed kernel-enforced over 200 plant-then-write rounds.

title: Re-enable CI and cut Actions minute burn
description:
CI (.github/workflows/ci.yml) was disabled_manually ~2026-03-25 because Actions minutes were being exhausted on this private repo. Result: ~4 months of pushes to main with zero automated verification. All four gates (typos, dprint, fmt, clippy, tests) pass locally on main today, so the workflow should go green once re-enabled.

Re-enable it, and reduce per-run cost so the credit problem does not recur:
- Skip runs for beads-only commits (9 of last 19 commits touched only .beads/issues.jsonl, each firing a full 5-job run).
- Consolidate 5 jobs into 2 to stop paying per-job minute rounding and a duplicated Rust compile across the clippy and build-and-test runners.
acceptance_criteria: CI workflow is enabled; a run on main completes green; per-run billable minutes reduced; beads-only commits do not trigger a run.

title: MCP apply defaults auto_accept=true — silently overwrites divergent configs (data loss)
description: selfie_apply_dotfiles (MCP) defaults auto_accept=true, which auto-accepts DeployDecision::Conflict and overwrites the target (service.rs:661). A Conflict happens when a target exists, has no local deploy-state (NotTracked), and its content DIFFERS from the repo source — exactly the fresh-second-machine case (e.g. deploying home's configs onto the work machine, which has its own unpushed edits). Result: the other machine's config is silently clobbered with NO prompt. This violates the 'no silent failures / no data loss' principle and is worst on the AI-native path (the primary use case). Fix: when there is no interactive resolver (MCP/headless), the SAFE default must be to SKIP conflicts and report them (auto_accept=false), requiring explicit opt-in to overwrite. Consider also surfacing the diff in the conflict event so an AI/user can decide. Surfaced 2026-07-23 reasoning through cross-machine deploy safety.
close_reason: MCP apply now defaults auto_accept=false; conflicts skipped+reported with diff. Fixed in 3238cd6, test apply_param_defaults_auto_accept_to_false
