title: Investigate whether CLI path flags actually override the config file
description:
OBSERVED, NOT DIAGNOSED -- needs confirming before it is treated as a bug.

While attempting an end-to-end CLI run inside a temporary fixture, an agent reported that the selfie binary picked up the USER'S REAL config and package directory despite being passed -p / --dotfiles-directory / --state-directory, and enumerated the user's actual dotfiles. It reported '0 deployed, 8 skipped', so nothing was written and no harm was done, and the agent aborted rather than retrying.

If that reproduces, it means CLI path flags do not take precedence over the config file, which is both a usability bug and a testing hazard: any attempt to exercise the real binary against a fixture would silently operate on the developer's own configuration instead. The '8 skipped' suggests it read the real dotfiles directory.

TO INVESTIGATE:
- Do -p / --dotfiles-directory / --state-directory actually override ~/.config/selfie/config.yml, or are they merged the other way round?
- Is the precedence documented in docs/configuration.md, and does the documentation match the code?
- Does an env var or a default path win over an explicit flag anywhere?
- Check crates/cli/src/config.rs and wherever CliConfig is assembled from clap matches plus the config file.

If flags do win and the agent's run was misconfigured, close this and record what actually happened -- a false alarm here is worth the same write-up as a real bug, because the next person to try an end-to-end CLI test will hit the same question.

Reported by the selfie-ywvs code reviewer as a process note; explicitly NOT claimed by it as a finding, and not investigated.

title: Fold credential redaction into BoundedText and retire GitMessage's git framing
description:
GitMessage (crates/selfie/src/git/message.rs), added by PR #83 for selfie-cvpm, is:

    BoundedText::bound(redact_credentials(text))

redact_credentials is NOT git-specific. It is RFC 3986 userinfo redaction over whitespace-delimited tokens: any scheme, scp-style user@host:path, IPv6 authorities, query parameters, insteadOf-style config values. Nothing in it knows what git is. The only git-specific things in that file are the type name, the module path, some test names, and a doc line about git's stderr not being UTF-8.

BoundedText truncates and does NOT redact. So the redaction currently sits behind a git-shaped door while FIVE non-git sites forward untrusted text through the bound-only path:

  resolve.rs:292  provider command stderr   <- THE CREDENTIAL PATH
  resolve.rs:283  provider command error
  event.rs:894 and :1739  CommandFailure::ExecutionFailed.stderr -> CLI and MCP JSON
  audit.rs:317   audit command stderr
  audit.rs:340   audit command error

A user's command that fails while contacting https://user:token@api.example.com therefore has that URL bounded and forwarded verbatim to the terminal and to an AI assistant's transcript. That is precisely the class selfie-cvpm closed, left open everywhere except git.

DECIDED (maintainer, 2026-07-31): fold the redaction INTO BoundedText so bound() redacts-then-truncates. All five sites are then fixed by construction with no call-site changes, and there is no second type anyone can reach for by mistake -- the failure mode this codebase keeps hitting. Rename the type accordingly; 'Bounded' undersells it once it sanitizes.

ORDER IS LOAD-BEARING: redact THEN truncate. Truncating first can cut a URL mid-string, leaving 'https://user:TOK' with no '@' to anchor on, so the bound would manufacture a leak the redactor can no longer see. PR #83 has a test pinning this (the fixture arithmetic is spelled out because it was vacuous on the first attempt); carry that test over.

GitMessage then collapses to a thin alias or disappears. Check what remains genuinely git-specific -- from_stderr's lossy decode is generic, and the git/ module keeps only the error types.

COSTS TO STATE:
- Over-redaction spreads: git@github.com becomes ***@github.com, and identity-error emails go, at five more sites. Deliberate everywhere else already; the reasoning is that deciding a username is safe is an allowlist that fails open.
- Five sites change behavior. Each needs a test that a credential in that path's text is redacted, with a positive control that non-credential text survives byte-identical.
- PR #83's 14 mutations cover the redactor; re-run them after the move rather than assuming they survive it.

Also fold in the rename of the redaction's residual documentation: the covered/uncovered lists in message.rs and docs/sync.md are written as git-specific and would become general.

Raised by the maintainer reviewing PR #83: 'is it really just for dealing with git? ...if it's used to handle strings that could have nothing to do with git, i think it could/should be renamed.' Verified: it is generic, and five non-git sites are currently walking past it.

title: tcsh and csh users cannot run any login-shell command path
description:
ShellCommandRunner::login_shell (crates/selfie/src/commands/shell.rs:83-93) is std::env::var("SHELL").unwrap_or_else(|_| Self::default_shell()) with login: true, and build_command (:104-108) adds -l unconditionally. There is no shell-family handling anywhere.

tcsh and csh REJECT -l alongside another flag. Measured on both:

  tcsh -l -c 'printf %s hello'  ->  Unknown option: `-l'   rc=1
  csh  -l -c 'printf %s hello'  ->  Unknown option: `-l'   rc=1
  tcsh    -c 'printf %s hello'  ->  hello                  rc=0

Their usage lines confirm -l is accepted only as the sole argument.

So for a user whose $SHELL is /bin/tcsh or /bin/csh, EVERY login-runner path fails: install, check, audit and apply, in BOTH the CLI (create_command_runner, cli/src/commands/common.rs:64-65) and the MCP server (server.rs:229, main.rs:65). Not a degraded experience -- rc=1 on every command that runs anything.

Pre-existing and unrelated to selfie-evf9; found while measuring shell behavior for that unit's fence design, and confirmed independently by its plan reviewer.

Fix direction: drop -l for the csh family. Their login profiles (.login, .cshrc) are not usable through -l -c anyway, so the flag buys nothing there -- csh sources .cshrc for non-interactive shells regardless. Detect by the shell's basename rather than by probing, and note that selfie-evf9's stdout fence uses POSIX 'trap ... EXIT' and 'printf', neither of which csh has, so a csh-family path needs its own decision about content commands or an explicit refusal.

Consider whether an unsupported $SHELL should fail with a clear message naming the shell rather than surfacing the shell's own 'Unknown option' text.

title: apply records a deployment for a symlinked target it never wrote to
description:
crates/selfie/src/dotfile_service/service.rs:1337: when drift == NotTracked and !options.dry_run, apply calls record_deployment(...) -- including for a target it has just REFUSED to write because the target is a symlink.

Measured: symlinked target, no prior state, destination content equal to the repo file. apply emits deployed_count=0, skipped_count=1 and writes nothing to the target, then records a deploy-state entry with source_checksum == deployed_checksum and a deployed_at timestamp. The state now asserts a deployment that did not occur.

SAME CLASS AS selfie-13bq -- 'the state file carries data implying a guarantee it does not provide' -- and the same lie that selfie-ywvs (P1) produces via track. Unit A of the target-semantics batch refuses track for exactly this reason, but leaves apply doing it by a different door.

CONSEQUENCE: it is the second manufacturer of the state that makes selfie-qvwq's diagnosis meaningless. Once that entry exists, drift compares live checksums against a recorded deployment that never happened, so the next edit to the repo file produces 'repo changed' forever with the target never updated.

There is an existing 25-line comment at service.rs:1286-1291 acknowledging this record and arguing it costs nothing. That argument predates the exfiltration chain in selfie-ywvs being understood and is worth re-examining: a state entry claiming a symlinked target was deployed is not free, it is what makes every later drift report wrong.

Fix direction: do not record a deployment for an entry that was refused. Check the interaction with selfie-13bq (which may remove the field the record relies on) and with the deliberate Skip-branch exclusion at service.rs:1305 before changing the condition.

Found by the unit-A plan reviewer while checking the plan's drift/apply parity claim.
notes:
WORSE THAN FILED, confirmed by probe (2026-07-31). The original note framed this as 'a second manufacturer' of the false state, alongside selfie-ywvs's track. It is more than that: APPLY MANUFACTURES IT ALONE, FROM THE MOST COMMON STARTING POINT, WITH NO track INVOLVED.

Measured: service.rs:1337 fires, save_deploy_state at service.rs:1435 runs unconditionally when !dry_run, and state/deploy-state.yml lands on disk with source_checksum == deployed_checksum for a symlinked target that was never written. drift on the next run returns [].

So the sequence is:
  fresh machine, config already symlinked into place by stow/yadm/Syncthing (selfie-qvwq row 1b)
  -> selfie apply: refuses to write, reports skipped, AND records a deployment
  -> state now says the symlinked target is deployed and in sync
  -> drift reports drift_count=0, 'in sync'
  -> user edits the repo file
  -> 'repo changed' FOREVER, apply refusing every round

That is selfie-qvwq's permanent-drift bug reached with no track command at all -- just apply, on the ordinary fresh-machine case. selfie-ywvs (P1) is one door into that state; this is the other, and it is the one a user hits by default.

The 25-line comment at service.rs:1286-1291 argues the record costs nothing. It does not: it is what makes every subsequent drift report wrong, and it converts a recoverable situation (nothing recorded, apply refuses and says why every time) into a silent one (recorded, drift says in sync, and the refusal only resurfaces after an unrelated edit).

Unit A of the target-semantics batch fixes track and leaves this deliberately untouched.

title: steps.rs renders a JoinError's Display, which includes the panic payload, into an event
description:
crates/selfie/src/package/service/steps.rs:150-153:

    if let Err(join_error) = output_task.await {
        sender.send_warning(format!("Output streaming task failed: {join_error}")).await;
    }

JoinError's Display renders the panic payload. Verified against tokio-1.53.1/src/runtime/task/error.rs:135-153 -- it writes 'task {id} panicked with message {payload:?}'.

The joined task is the one draining every decoded output chunk of a streaming install command (spawned at steps.rs:127). So if it panics while holding command output, the panic message -- which can be derived from that output -- goes into a PackageEvent warning, and from there to the CLI and the MCP server's JSON.

THIS IS THE SAME LEAK CLASS the selfie library already guards against in commands/shell.rs, where join_read deliberately inspects a JoinError for is_cancelled() and DROPS it, substituting a fixed &'static str, precisely because 'the panic payload comes from the task that was holding this command's output, so it can be derived from a credential'. That guard was added in PR #81 after a plan reviewer caught the exposure.

One file away, on the streaming path, the same shape has no guard and no test.

Independent of selfie-6bav: it predates that unit and survives it. 6bav removes tokio::spawn from shell.rs, which is why 'no panic payload can reach PackageEvent::Completed' will be true of run_buffered and FALSE of selfie as a whole. Whoever writes that PR body must not overclaim.

Fix direction: mirror shell.rs's join_read -- read is_cancelled()/is_panic() and emit a fixed message, never the JoinError itself. Cheap. Add the assert_secret_free test that shell.rs's equivalent has.

Found by the selfie-6bav plan reviewer while verifying whether deleting shell.rs's panic-payload tests was safe.

title: Streamed output corrupts multi-byte UTF-8 characters at chunk boundaries
description:
crates/selfie/src/commands/shell.rs:616 (on branch fix/selfie-ql8m-...; the equivalent line exists on main) does:

    let chunk = String::from_utf8_lossy(&buffer[..n]).to_string();

Reads are chunked at arbitrary 1024-byte read-syscall boundaries. When a multi-byte UTF-8 character straddles a boundary, from_utf8_lossy replaces its fragments -- and it happens in the PRODUCER, so the damage is irreversible before any consumer sees it.

MEASURED (U2's prototype harness, input = 1023 'a' bytes then 'e-acute' then 'b' bytes):
  3 chunks; joined output contains U+FFFD = true; contains the original character = false
  chunk 0: len=1026 tail=['\u{FFFD}', 'a', 'a']
  chunk 1: len=3    tail=['\u{FFFD}']
ONE character becomes TWO replacement characters.

Reaches the user two ways, both already live:
- CLI: crates/cli/src/event_processor.rs:372 prints the already-corrupted String
- MCP: crates/mcp-server/src/event_collector.rs:136 puts it straight into the JSON an AI assistant reads

Both see a String, not bytes, so neither can repair it.

Scope is STREAMING ONLY. CommandOutput.stdout() accumulates raw bytes separately and is unaffected, which is why no existing test caught this -- the buffered path is byte-exact and the streaming path is not, and nothing compares them.

Any package whose install command emits non-ASCII output hits this: accented package names, box-drawing progress output, emoji in a formatter's summary, any localized message.

FIX: U2 (selfie-6bav) fixes this as part of replacing the hand-rolled streaming loop, using a small Decoder that holds an incomplete trailing sequence in the buffer until it completes. Note both obvious codecs are wrong and were measured: LinesCodec ERRORS on non-UTF-8 (tokio-util-0.7.19/src/codec/lines_codec.rs:95) and aborts the stream; BytesCodec chunks at the same read-syscall boundaries and fixes nothing.

Verified by U2's author against a prototype; the fix must keep CommandOutput.stdout() byte-exact (accumulating decoded text instead of raw bytes would silently make the buffered path lossy -- a fresh bug introduced by the fix).
close_reason: Closed

title: ShellCommandRunner hand-rolls process I/O that tokio and tokio-util already provide
description:
RAISED BY THE USER while reviewing PR #81: are we reinventing wheels? Investigated; substantially yes, confined to the process-I/O plumbing inside crates/selfie/src/commands/shell.rs. CLAUDE.md's own guidance is to 'lean towards using third party libraries for substantial features and functionality, so we can keep the codebase small'.

FOUR CONCRETE OVERLAPS, each verified against dependency source rather than reputation:

1. run_buffered (~80 lines: two tokio::spawn'd readers + select! + join) IS tokio::process::Child::wait_with_output(). From tokio-1.53.1/src/process/mod.rs:1446, it does try_join3(self.wait(), stdout_fut, stderr_fut) -- the concurrent read-and-wait that avoids the ~64KB pipe-buffer deadlock is exactly try_join3.

   MOST IMPORTANTLY: tokio's inner read is 'crate::io::util::read_to_end(io, &mut vec).await?' and try_join3 short-circuits on Err. SO selfie-ql8m -- the P1 fixed in PR #81, where 'let _ = read_to_end(...)' discarded a read error and returned a partial buffer as complete -- COULD NOT HAVE EXISTED had run_buffered called wait_with_output(). We hand-wrote the bug that the library does not have.

   Why it was hand-rolled: wait_with_output(mut self) CONSUMES the Child, so the timeout and cancellation arms cannot call child.kill(). The idiomatic answer is Command::kill_on_drop(true) (tokio mod.rs:664) plus tokio::time::timeout / select!, dropping the future to kill the child. Verify that drop-kills-mid-wait_with_output actually holds before relying on it.

2. execute_streaming's ~130-line loop -- manual read(&mut buf) into fixed 1024-byte buffers, a hand-rolled stdout_done/stderr_done/process_done state machine, and exit_status.unwrap() guarded only by a comment (that is selfie-t0nb, which exists ONLY because of this state machine) -- is what tokio_util::codec::FramedRead gives you as a Stream. tokio-util is ALREADY a workspace dependency (Cargo.toml) with features = ['rt'] for CancellationToken; this needs the 'codec' feature added, not a new dependency.

3. The dropped-chunk bug (selfie-qd3r and selfie-z6cr, the whole of U2's scope) is try_send on a bounded channel discarding chunks with no marker. A real Stream has backpressure semantics by construction. Patching try_send may be solving a problem that the right abstraction does not have.

4. Killing a command whose GRANDCHILD inherited the pipe (selfie-b7mv, P2) is process-group management -- command-group / process-wrap. child.kill() only ever kills the direct child. This is a solved problem with a crate, not something to hand-roll.

NOT wheel-reinvention, and should stay: the CommandRunner trait itself (the hexagonal port), login-shell selection, and the mapping of failures onto domain errors and PackageEvents.

BEFORE ACTING, verify against source (.claude/rules/verification.md -- three claims about a crate's behavior were wrong here before, one in the unsafe direction):
- does dropping a wait_with_output future with kill_on_drop(true) reliably kill, and does it reap?
- does FramedRead compose with the timeout and cancellation arms without reintroducing a hand-rolled select!?
- what does process-wrap actually guarantee on macOS vs Linux, and is its maintenance status acceptable?
- chunking at arbitrary 1024-byte boundaries can split a multibyte UTF-8 character; check whether any consumer lossy-decodes per chunk and turns it into U+FFFD. Line-framing would avoid it. NOT yet verified -- check before claiming.

INTERACTION WITH OPEN WORK: this potentially subsumes selfie-qd3r, selfie-z6cr, selfie-b7mv and selfie-t0nb rather than each being patched separately. Sequence it against them deliberately rather than doing both.
notes:
SCOPE DECISION (2026-07-30, user): this becomes the primary bead for U2 of the command-execution batch, replacing that unit's original narrow scope.

U2 was queued to PATCH selfie-qd3r/selfie-z6cr -- add a marker so a dropped streamed chunk is visible. The user chose the migration instead, on the reasoning that a real Stream has backpressure semantics by construction, so the marker patch would be thrown away by the migration that follows it.

SUBSUMES (verify each is actually closed before closing it -- do not assume the migration covers them):
- selfie-qd3r and selfie-z6cr (P2, duplicates of each other): try_send silently dropping streamed chunks.
- selfie-t0nb (P3): exit_status.unwrap() guarded only by a comment. It exists ONLY because the hand-rolled loop needs a stdout_done/stderr_done/process_done state machine; a Stream-based rewrite has no such variable to unwrap.

MAY subsume, planner's call after investigating process-wrap/command-group:
- selfie-b7mv (P2): run_buffered can hang past its own timeout when a grandchild inherits the pipe. This is process-group killing. Whether it belongs in this unit or stays separate depends on whether a new dependency is warranted -- decide deliberately, do not absorb it silently.

Sequencing: U2 rewrites run_buffered, which PR #81 (selfie-ql8m) just fixed. Plan against PR #81's branch, not main, and land after it merges.
SCOPE CORRECTED BY MEASUREMENT (2026-07-30). The note above claimed this unit subsumes selfie-qd3r and selfie-z6cr. THAT IS MEASURABLY WRONG and the claim is retracted.

THE HYPOTHESIS WAS: a real Stream gives backpressure by construction, so a dropped chunk becomes impossible rather than merely marked.

IT IS FALSE. The bounded channel is created by the CALLER, not the adapter -- crates/selfie/src/package/service/steps.rs:121, capacity 1000 -- and handed to the adapter as an mpsc::Sender<OutputChunk> through the port. Whatever the adapter reads WITH, it must still push INTO someone else's bounded channel. A Stream inside the adapter changes nothing about that.

Measured, not reasoned: U2's prototype with the full rewrite in place, run against a deliberately slow consumer on a 4-slot channel, still dropped 5003 chunks.

So selfie-qd3r and selfie-z6cr stay OPEN and unaddressed by this unit. Their fix is a drop counter plus an end-of-stream event -- qd3r's own 'cheapest first' option -- which needs a new PackageEvent variant and a port-doc change, and is its own unit.

The genuinely structural fix for those two would be changing the PORT to return impl Stream, which would give real backpressure. That changes the hexagonal port, mockall::automock, and four hand-written doubles, for one production caller. Explicitly rejected for this unit; recorded as the honest long-term answer.

WHAT THIS UNIT DOES CLOSE, each verified by prototype rather than argued:
- selfie-t0nb (P3) -- by construction. The exit status becomes the value of an expression; there is no Option to unwrap.
- selfie-b7mv (P2) -- by construction. Reads and wait become one future under one deadline. Measured: Err(Timeout) at 2.0029s, versus wait() returning in 2.79ms today and the reader join then blocking 8.0089s past a deadline that no longer exists.
- selfie-x12u (P2, filed today) -- streamed output corrupting multi-byte UTF-8 at chunk boundaries. Real, user-visible, reaching both the terminal and the MCP JSON.

ALSO CORRECTED: claim (1) in the note above is half true. tokio's wait_with_output() has the right ALGORITHM (try_join3, which short-circuits -- so selfie-ql8m genuinely could not have existed against it) but the wrong API: it returns one untagged io::Result<Output> and cannot distinguish a stdout read failure from a stderr read failure from a wait() failure. PR #81 built exactly those three distinctions, they are public API (OutputStream is re-exported and consumed by test-common), and three tests assert them. Adopting wait_with_output() literally would DELETE that. Use its algorithm with our own typed futures instead.

Stale line numbers for whoever picks this up: qd3r cites shell.rs:473 and z6cr cites :465; on base bb112df the try_send is at shell.rs:618.
close_reason: Closed

title: Whole-file provider content has no structure detector, while vars bindings do
description:
resolve.rs:221-228 warns when a vars binding's value contains a line break: 'dotfile var X contains a line break; it will be substituted as-is'. The comment above it says why -- values are spliced verbatim, so a line break can add structure the template author did not intend.

The whole-file Provider branch has no equivalent. Its content is the command's entire stdout, written to the target unchanged, with only two gates: bytes.is_empty() and bytes.len() > MAX_CONTENT_BYTES (8 MiB).

That asymmetry matters because the Provider path is where the worse hazard actually lands. Per selfie-evf9 (P1), a login profile that writes to stdout gets spliced into resolved content -- and a spliced banner in a VARS binding produces a warning naming the binding, while the same banner on the WHOLE-FILE path produces nothing at all. The guarded path is the one that needed guarding less.

Fix direction: not obvious, and worth thinking about rather than pattern-matching the vars warning. A line break in whole-file content is entirely normal -- most dotfiles have many -- so the vars heuristic does not transfer. Candidates: warn when the content's first line looks like shell/profile chatter; run a control command (':' or 'true') under the same shell and warn if IT produces stdout, which detects a noisy profile directly and is the most precise signal available; or let a package declare an expected shape.

Note the control-command idea would also close selfie-evf9's detection half, so consider them together.

Found by the selfie-w8gd/selfie-fbwo plan reviewer (U3 of the command-execution batch).

title: Audit dotfile_service_tests for assertions that pass through the conflict path
description:
During selfie-ql8m (U1 of the command-execution batch), two newly written tests -- a_provider_whose_output_could_not_be_read_leaves_a_pre_existing_target_intact and its binding twin -- did NOT bite under mutation M7. Cause: they ran with ApplyOptions::default(), which carries no conflict resolver. A secret-bearing entry whose target content differs is then reported as a CONFLICT and skipped, so the pre-existing target survived for a reason with nothing to do with the read failure under test. A truncated credential written down that path would have been equally invisible.

The tests asserted a true fact for a false reason. Fixed in that PR by routing both through accepting() and seeding the control to match, so control and assertion take the same path.

THE CONCERN IS THE OTHER ~45 TESTS IN crates/selfie/tests/dotfile_service_tests.rs. Any pre-existing secret-bearing test that seeds a DIFFERING target under ApplyOptions::default() has the same shape: it takes the conflict path, never reaches the behavior it was written for, and cannot observe a resolve-side regression. The U1 author fixed only the two it wrote and explicitly did not audit the rest.

This is verbatim the third of the four vacuous tests catalogued in .claude/rules/testing.md ('the target was seeded with different content, so the test took the conflict path and never reached the skip it was written for') -- which means the pattern has now been found twice in this file, independently. That is the argument for a sweep rather than spot fixes.

Approach: for each secret-bearing test that seeds a pre-existing target, check whether ApplyOptions carries a resolver, and whether the assertion could pass via the conflict path. Prove each one can fail by mutating the behavior it claims to test -- reading is not sufficient here; both known instances were invisible to reading and found only by mutation.

Found while fixing selfie-ql8m.

title: run_git has no timeout and can hang an MCP tool indefinitely
description:
crates/selfie/src/git/adapter.rs:82 calls Command::output(), which blocks indefinitely. A remote that accepts the TCP connection and then never responds hangs the call forever.

Every network git operation goes through run_git -- push (:455), fetch (:472) -- so a wedged or hostile remote hangs 'selfie sync push' / 'selfie sync pull' with no bound.

The asymmetry is the point: command_timeout already exists in config and is threaded through CommandRunner for every user-authored package command, but it is not applied to git. The one place selfie talks to the network is the one place with no deadline. GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0 and Stdio::null() at adapter.rs:80-81 show the non-interactive hang case was considered for stdin; the network case was not.

Worse via MCP than via CLI: a CLI user sees a hang and hits Ctrl+C. An MCP client gets a tool call that never returns.

Fix direction: run git under a deadline. Note the CommandRunner path already solved this shape (spawn + tokio::select! on a timeout, killing the child) -- but run_git is sync std::process inside blocking_git, so it needs either the same treatment natively or a wait-with-timeout. Consider whether it should share command_timeout or get its own config key, since a large fetch legitimately takes longer than a package check.

Found by the selfie-cvpm plan reviewer (U4 of the command-execution batch) while reviewing the git adapter's failure paths.

title: run_buffered can hang past its own timeout once child.wait() resolves
description:
crates/selfie/src/commands/shell.rs:169-198. The timeout and cancellation arms live INSIDE the tokio::select!. Once child.wait() wins that race the select! is over and its deadline is gone, but the very next lines await stdout_handle and stderr_handle with no deadline at all.

child.kill() also only kills the direct child. So a command that spawns a grandchild inheriting the stdout pipe -- sh -c 'daemon &' is the ordinary shape -- leaves the write end of the pipe open after the shell exits. wait() returns, read_to_end never reaches EOF, and the join blocks forever, past a command_timeout the user explicitly configured.

Pre-existing and independent of selfie-ql8m: today's .unwrap_or_default() awaits hang on exactly the same line, and ql8m's fix (propagating the read error) does not change the reachability.

Fix direction: bound the post-wait join, e.g. tokio::time::timeout on the join for the remainder of the command_timeout budget, and decide what the result is when the reader is still live at the deadline -- that is a genuine design question, since output read so far may be complete or may not be, and ql8m establishes that a partial buffer must never be reported as whole.

Found independently by the selfie-ql8m plan author and its reviewer (U1 of the command-execution batch); verified by the lead.
notes:
SEVERITY UNDERSTATED BY THIS BEAD'S TITLE, and the scope is wider than filed. Measured by the selfie-6bav plan reviewer with a 2-SECOND timeout:

  buffered:  elapsed=8.011s  result=Ok(Ok(8))
  streaming: elapsed=8.017s  timed_out=false

The results are Ok, not Err(Timeout). The timeout is not merely EXCEEDED -- it is UNENFORCED, and a command the caller bounded to 2s is reported back as a SUCCESS after 8s. That is a wrong-answer bug, not a latency bug. 'Can hang past its own timeout' undersells it.

ALSO: this is NOT run_buffered-only. execute_streaming has the identical shape -- the 'if !process_done' guards at shell.rs:432/440 disarm the timeout and cancellation arms once wait() resolves, exactly as the buffered select! does. So the bead spans both functions.

CONSEQUENCE FOR selfie-6bav: that unit ships as two commits, streaming then buffered. Commit 1 closes the streaming half and commit 2 the buffered half. DO NOT CLOSE THIS BEAD ON COMMIT 1 ALONE -- if commit 2 is dropped, this stays open.
close_reason: Closed

title: check.rs renders a CommandError unbounded where audit.rs bounds the identical expression
description:
crates/selfie/src/package/service/check.rs:282 builds CheckResult::Error(err.to_string()) from a CommandError with no bound.

audit.rs:335 bounds the IDENTICAL expression via BoundedText::bound(err.to_string().as_bytes()).into_string(), and carries this comment explaining why:

  'Bounded for the same reason as the non-zero-exit arm above, and with the same
   expression resolve.rs's run_capture bounds: no CommandError variant's Display
   prints process output, but every one embeds the package file's own command:
   string, which is unbounded. Treating two identical expressions differently is
   how the gap in the arm above went unnoticed.'

check.rs is that same untreated expression. The reasoning in audit's comment applies verbatim: no CommandError variant Display-prints process output, but every variant embeds the package file's own command: string, which the user authors and which is unbounded.

Egress path is real, not theoretical: CheckResult::Error flows into OperationFailure::CommandError(InvalidCommand { reason }) at check.rs:189-197, and on to both the CLI and the MCP server's JSON.

Fix: bound it the way audit.rs does. Consider whether the two sites should share a helper so a third consumer cannot diverge again -- the comment predicted this exact failure mode and it happened anyway one file over.

Found by the selfie-ql8m plan reviewer (U1 of the command-execution batch); verified against the tree by the lead.

title: Streamed output chunks are silently dropped under backpressure
description:
shell.rs:473 sends each streamed chunk with 'let _ = output_sender.try_send(...)' against a 1000-slot channel. When the consumer falls behind, try_send fails and the chunk is discarded with no marker, no counter and no event.

The user watching 'selfie package install' output cannot tell the stream is incomplete. Output simply has a hole in it. For an install log that is the difference between 'the command printed nothing alarming' and 'I did not see what it printed.'

History confirms the non-blocking choice was DELIBERATE, not an oversight: 1d6e996 used a blocking 'tx.send().await', 9891f05 switched to non-blocking try_send. Blocking the command's output pump on a slow consumer is worse. So the bug is not try_send — it is that the drop is unmarked.

Found by selfie-3hap's author while documenting the port. That branch now DOCUMENTS the behavior on both the trait and the adapter; it does not fix it. So the gap is disclosed but still silent at runtime.

Options, cheapest first:
  - Count drops and emit one event at end of stream ('N chunks omitted').
  - Insert a sentinel chunk at the drop point so the hole is visible in place.
  - Grow or make the channel unbounded (moves the failure to memory).

Prefer something that tells the user, since this project's whole premise is running arbitrary user-authored commands against their environment.
acceptance_criteria: A consumer can determine that streamed output was incomplete.
notes:
SUPERSEDED IN APPROACH by selfie-6bav (2026-07-30, user decision). Not closed -- the defect is real and still open -- but the fix is no longer 'add a marker to the try_send drop'. A tokio_util Stream-based rewrite of execute_streaming has backpressure semantics by construction, so the marker patch would be discarded by the migration. Close this only when 6bav demonstrably makes a dropped chunk impossible or visible; verify rather than assume.
NOT CLOSED BY selfie-6bav -- hypothesis disproven by measurement (2026-07-30). The earlier note said the Stream rewrite would make the drop impossible by construction. It does not: the bounded channel is created by the CALLER at package/service/steps.rs:121 and handed to the adapter through the port, so the adapter must still push into someone else's bounded channel regardless of what it reads with. U2's prototype, with the full rewrite in place and a slow consumer on a 4-slot channel, still dropped 5003 chunks. This bead stands on its own and needs the drop counter plus an end-of-stream event.

title: Git stderr goes unbounded into GitSyncError and can carry a token in a remote URL
description:
crates/selfie/src/git/adapter.rs:88-95 puts git's stderr, unbounded, into GitSyncError::OperationFailed { message }.

Git echoes the remote URL in many failure messages, and an HTTPS remote can embed credentials — 'https://user:TOKEN@host/repo.git' is a shape people really use. A push or fetch failure would then carry that token into the error, and from there wherever the error is rendered.

Same shape as selfie-iuhz (unbounded command stderr entering a diagnostic) but outside the package-command frame: this is the git adapter, not CommandRunner, so it is not covered by the truncate_stderr rule in .claude/rules/secrets.md and would not be covered by the BoundedText type selfie-iuhz introduces unless someone deliberately extends it there.

Two separable concerns:
  - The bound. Route it through the same bound the command paths use, once selfie-iuhz lands and BoundedText is pub.
  - The credential. A bound does not help if the token is in the first 2000 bytes, which it will be. Consider redacting a userinfo component from any URL appearing in a git error, which is a different and more targeted fix.

The second matters more. Found while planning selfie-iuhz.
acceptance_criteria: A git failure message cannot carry credentials from a remote URL, and its stderr is bounded.
notes:
ESCALATED TO P2 and CONFIRMED REACHING MCP by the selfie-iuhz plan reviewer. The bead as filed treated the MCP path as uncertain. It is not:

  git/adapter.rs:88-95        git's full stderr into GitSyncError::OperationFailed { message }
  sync_service/service.rs:205 converts via SyncError::GitError(other.to_string())
  -> surfaces through the selfie_sync_push and selfie_sync_pull MCP tools

So a git auth failure carrying 'https://user:TOKEN@host/repo.git' reaches an AI assistant's transcript, unbounded and unredacted.

CRITICAL: TRUNCATION DOES NOT FIX THIS. A credential embedded in a remote URL appears in the FIRST bytes of git's message, so any length bound — including the BoundedText type selfie-iuhz introduces — passes it through intact. This needs REDACTION of the userinfo component, which BoundedText deliberately does not do (it truncates; it does not sanitize, which is why 'UntrustedText' was rejected as a name for it).

Do not close this by routing git errors through the command-path bound. That would look like a fix and change nothing.
REPRO CORRECTED BY THE U4 PLAN AUTHOR, pending independent confirmation (git 2.50.1, local-only fixture: loopback listener + refused port, no network egress).

THE EXAMPLE IN THIS BEAD'S DESCRIPTION DOES NOT REPRODUCE ON CURRENT GIT. Tested:
  https://user:PASS@127.0.0.1:1/o/r.git   push, connect refused -> 'fatal: unable to access https://127.0.0.1:1/o/r.git/' -- userinfo STRIPPED by git
  https://TOKEN@127.0.0.1:1/...           fetch, connect refused -> STRIPPED
  http://user:PASS@127.0.0.1:8731/...     fetch, server 401      -> 'Authentication failed for http://127.0.0.1:8731/o/r.git/' -- STRIPPED

THE SHAPE THAT ACTUALLY LEAKS is token-as-username on the credential-prompt path:
  http://TOKEN@127.0.0.1:8731/...  fetch, server 401
  -> fatal: could not read Password for 'http://Zk9qP2mW7xR4tL6vB1nH3jD5@127.0.0.1:8731': terminal prompts disabled
  -> TOKEN VERBATIM.

That is exactly the GitHub PAT idiom (https://ghp_xxx@github.com/o/r.git) that 'gh auth setup-git' and most CI docs produce, so it is the common case rather than an exotic one.

SELFIE'S OWN HARDENING IS WHAT OPENS THE PATH. run_git sets GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0 (adapter.rs:81). That is why git reaches 'could not read Password for <url-with-username>' instead of prompting. The MCP server is precisely the non-interactive caller that setting exists for. The mitigation created the exposure.

Also found: transfer.credentialsInUrl=warn redacts the password half and prints the USERNAME verbatim -- so with the token-as-username shape the token is printed twice.

The fix remains warranted and is stronger for this: without it we depend on an external binary's undocumented, version-dependent redaction, and older git (CI images, LTS distros) strips less. Not verified on git < 2.50.1 -- no claim made about 2.39.

ANYONE WRITING THE PR BODY: do not repeat this bead's original example. It is false on current git.
CORRECTION TO THE NOTE ABOVE, from the U4 plan reviewer's independent reproduction (git 2.50.1 Apple Git-155, its own loopback fixture on both 127.0.0.1 and ::1).

THE CLAIM 'SELFIE'S OWN HARDENING IS WHAT OPENS THE PATH' IS FALSE. RETRACTED.

The reviewer reproduced the same leak with GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT UNSET:
  fatal: could not read Password for 'http://Zk9qP2mW7xR4tL6vB1nH3jD5@127.0.0.1:55007': Device not configured

GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0 changes only the trailing clause -- 'terminal prompts disabled' instead of 'Device not configured'. ANY non-interactive git (no tty, no working askpass) reaches the same 'could not read Password for <url-with-username>' message. run_git's GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0 at adapter.rs:81 is not the cause and removing it would not help.

Do not repeat the retracted claim in a PR body or commit message.

EVERYTHING ELSE IN THE NOTE ABOVE STANDS and was independently confirmed:
- https://user:PASS@host in a failure message is STRIPPED by git 2.50.1 -- this bead's original example does not reproduce
- token-as-username (http://TOKEN@host) leaks VERBATIM via 'could not read Password for ...', on BOTH fetch AND push (push matters -- it is the MCP-facing path)
- the same leak occurs over IPv6: ...for 'http://TOKEN@[::1]:PORT'...
- transfer.credentialsInUrl=warn redacts the password half and prints the username verbatim

Also independently confirmed, and it decides the fix's approach: gix-url 0.36.2's redacting Display (src/impls.rs) sets password = Some("redacted") and LEAVES user UNTOUCHED -- and when password is None, which is exactly the token-as-username case, it prints the URL entirely unmodified. gix-url's own docs say so: 'Beware that some URLs still print secrets if they use them outside of the designated password fields.' A gix::Url-based fix would pass a user:pass test and leak every GitHub PAT.
close_reason: Closed

title: Streamed install output is silently dropped under backpressure
description:
crates/selfie/src/commands/shell.rs:465 relays each chunk of a streaming command's output with 'let _ = output_sender.try_send(output_type(chunk));' against a bounded channel of capacity 1000 (crates/selfie/src/package/service/steps.rs:121).

try_send on a full channel returns Err and the chunk is discarded. The user watching an install therefore sees output with gaps, in no way marked as incomplete, whenever the consumer falls behind a fast-producing command — which is exactly when output is voluminous enough to matter.

The history makes this pointed. That send USED to report the failure: the initial commit (56051e5) had '.map_err(|e| CommandError::Callback(e.0))?' at what is now that line, and CommandError::Callback exists precisely to carry a dropped chunk. Commit 9891f05 ('Package install', 2025-07-12) replaced the propagation with a discard and orphaned the variant.

selfie-3hap deletes that now-dead variant — correctly, since its Display leaks raw command output — but doing so makes the reporting gap permanent rather than merely dormant. Filing so the gap is tracked on its own rather than disappearing with the variant.

Options: surface a marker in the stream when a chunk is dropped ('... output truncated, N chunks dropped'), grow or unbound the channel, or apply backpressure by awaiting send rather than try_send (which risks stalling the command). Note the third interacts with the pipe-deadlock avoidance in run_buffered.

Found while planning selfie-3hap.
acceptance_criteria: A dropped chunk of streamed output is either impossible or visible to the user, not silently absent.
notes:
Confirmed independently by the selfie-3hap plan reviewer, with the design constraint that makes it non-trivial: handle_chunked_read_result_streaming is a SYNC fn and therefore cannot .await a send, which is why try_send is used. Exact site is shell.rs:473 (earlier note said 465); channel is mpsc::channel::<OutputChunk>(1000) at steps.rs:121, and the consumer at steps.rs:127-138 forwards each chunk through sender_clone.send_info(...).await — so a slow event sink backs the channel up and chunks vanish with no marker.

The reviewer's recommendation, which I am following: file alongside the selfie-3hap PR rather than in it, since 3hap is what forecloses the old reporting route (CommandError::Callback was literally how 56051e5 reported this).
SUPERSEDED IN APPROACH by selfie-6bav (2026-07-30, user decision). Same as selfie-qd3r, which this duplicates. Close both together, and only after verifying 6bav actually closes them.
NOT CLOSED BY selfie-6bav -- same as selfie-qd3r, which this duplicates. Hypothesis disproven by measurement: 5003 chunks still dropped with the rewrite in place. See qd3r's note.

title: secrets.md mandates truncate_stderr but audit.rs violates it and two crates cannot call it
description:
selfie-ppp adds a rule to .claude/rules/secrets.md: 'truncate_stderr in commands/runner.rs is the one bound; call it rather than deciding a limit per site.' Two problems make that rule unfollowable as written.

1. AN EXISTING SITE ALREADY VIOLATES IT. crates/selfie/src/package/service/audit.rs:310-318 builds AuditResult::Error(format!("Audit command failed (exit code {exit_code}): {stderr}")) with the stderr UNBOUNDED. That value reaches the event stream and is serialized into the MCP JSON. Pre-existing, not introduced by selfie-ppp, and the same class the ppp bound exists to close.

2. TWO CRATES CANNOT OBEY IT. truncate_stderr is pub(crate) to selfie, so selfie-cli and selfie-mcp cannot call it — yet secrets.md's paths: frontmatter scopes the file to crates/cli/src/commands/track.rs among others. A reader in those crates is told to call a function they cannot reach.

Fix needs both halves: route audit.rs through the shared bound, and decide the visibility. If the rule is meant to apply outside selfie, truncate_stderr must be pub; if it is selfie-internal, the rule should say so and the adapters need their own guidance.

Found by the final reviewer on selfie-ppp.
acceptance_criteria: Every site that forwards a command's stderr goes through the shared bound, and the rule names a function its readers can call.
close_reason: Closed

title: Leak tests scan for the secret literal, so a Vec<u8> Debug of the same bytes goes undetected
description:
The repo's leak-regression tests assert that a secret string does not appear in formatted output — assert_no_event_mentions scans format!("{events:?}") for the literal.

Debug on Vec<u8> does not render the literal. It renders [115, 51, 99, ...]. So a leak that formats a bytes field with {:?} carries exactly the same secret material and passes every existing scan.

This is a live gap in the EXISTING tests, not a hypothetical one about future tests. ResolvedContent (crates/selfie/src/dotfile_service/resolve.rs:38) is 'pub bytes: Vec<u8>' on a pub(crate) struct — the type has no Display and a hand-written Debug printing '<N bytes>', which is real structural protection, but the field itself is reachable and a {:?} on it needs no string conversion at all.

FIX, and this is the part worth doing properly: have assert_no_event_mentions take the secret as BYTES and check both renderings itself — the literal and format!("{:?}", secret.as_bytes()) — so the choice is not re-made per test and the gap closes in the tests that already exist. Asserting both at each call site works but rebuilds the blind spot the next time someone adds a test.

Found while planning selfie-ppp; sharpened by that unit's plan reviewer.
acceptance_criteria: A Debug of a secret-bearing byte slice fails the leak-regression tests, not just a Debug of a secret string.
close_reason: Closed

title: No gate keeps Justfile recipes in sync with ci.yml, and they have drifted before
description:
selfie-blkr fixes the pre-commit-check skill by delegating to the Justfile, so the skill can no longer drift from the gates. That relocates the single point of failure rather than eliminating it: nothing checks that the Justfile's recipes still match .github/workflows/ci.yml.

This is not hypothetical. Commit 7c03c46 (PR #32, 2026-03-22) shipped a 'clippy' recipe WITHOUT '-- -D warnings' — selfie-blkr's exact bug, one layer down — and it was caught only by a Copilot review comment, then fixed in 61a0b77. Nothing would catch it today.

Known divergences right now, both currently harmless:
  - just fmt-check runs 'cargo fmt --check'; CI runs 'cargo fmt --all -- --check'. Verified equivalent in this virtual workspace (bare cargo fmt covers all members), so the strings differ but the behavior does not.
  - 'just check' omits typos and cargo build, which CI runs as separate jobs. Deliberate, and selfie-blkr now documents it in the skill.

Suggested fix: a test or CI step asserting the Justfile's gate recipes contain the same commands ci.yml runs. Parsing 'just -n <recipe>' output and comparing against the workflow's run: lines is cheap and catches the 7c03c46 class directly.

Found by the code review on selfie-blkr, which noted that the fix's own claim ('Justfile is the source of truth so this skill cannot drift') is true of skill-vs-Justfile drift and silent about Justfile-vs-CI drift.
acceptance_criteria: A weakened or diverged Justfile gate recipe is caught automatically rather than by a reviewer noticing.

title: Streamed command stdout is unconditional egress to both the terminal and MCP clients
description:
execute_command_streaming (crates/selfie/src/package/service/steps.rs:127-138) emits every line of a command's stdout as PackageEvent::Info { output: ConsoleOutput::Stdout(..) }, on success and on failure alike. Both adapters render it verbatim:
  - MCP: event_to_json serializes it as {"type":"output","text":...} (crates/mcp-server/src/event_collector.rs:133-139)
  - CLI: printed via println! (crates/cli/src/event_processor.rs:376-384)

Reproduced by the author of selfie-ppp: a command printing a secret to stdout put that secret in the MCP JSON.

Scope is 'selfie package install' only — check (check.rs:253) and audit (audit.rs:263) use the non-streaming execute path. That makes it narrower than selfie-ppp's framing but NOT smaller in consequence: for install, the stdout is fully public before any failure occurs, so selfie-ppp's fix to the failure-summary path does not touch it.

This is deliberately NOT a bug in the streaming feature itself — people want to watch 'brew install' run, and gutting that is not what selfie-ppp asks. The questions are:
  1. Should streamed command output be suppressible (a quiet flag, or off by default for commands marked as touching credentials)?
  2. Is streaming raw command output to an MCP client appropriate at all? A terminal is watched by the human who wrote the command; an MCP client is an AI agent with a transcript, and the trust model differs.

Found while tracing every exit for selfie-ppp; held out of that unit's scope deliberately.
acceptance_criteria: Streamed command output is either suppressible, or the decision to stream it unconditionally to both adapters is documented with its risk.
notes:
SCOPE WIDER THAN FILED, per the selfie-ppp plan reviewer:
  - The route carries STDERR as well as stdout — steps.rs:130 and :133 stream both as PackageEvent::Info, and event_to_json serializes both arms identically.
  - It fires on SUCCESS as well as failure, so a credential echoed by a command that then succeeds is exposed with no failure to draw attention to it.
  - 'install only' is slightly too strong: audit's stdout reaches MCP in parsed form as 'sources' (audit.rs:265-270 -> audit_details -> event_collector.rs:331-334). By design, but it is a second path. 'check' genuinely does not — check_status_label returns a fixed string.

That combination makes this the BROADEST exit described anywhere in .claude/rules/secrets.md: nothing on the path is truncated, redacted, or conditional. selfie-ppp adds a bullet to secrets.md naming it.

title: _dotfiles at package top level silently drops every dotfile in the package
description:
A package written with '_dotfiles:' instead of 'dotfiles:' loses every dotfile with no signal whatsoever.

Verified against bfff27b by the author of selfie-n310:
  pkg.validate(env).issues().all_issues()  ->  []            (validate reports NOTHING)
  apply  ->  Success(DotfilesApplied { deployed_count: 0, skipped_count: 0, steps_completed: 0/0 })

The user gets a successful run that did nothing, with no warning, no error, and no count indicating anything was skipped. Nothing distinguishes it from a package that legitimately has no dotfiles.

Cause: validate_unknown_fields (crates/selfie/src/package/validate.rs:238) skips ALL underscore-prefixed top-level keys, because the underscore prefix is how 826e854 made YAML anchors legal. Same class as selfie-kj5y, one level up: kj5y is an underscore key shadowing a known field INSIDE a dotfile entry, this is one shadowing a known field at the top level.

The fix is symmetric to kj5y's and about one line: flag a _-prefixed top-level key whose remainder appears in KNOWN_PACKAGE_FIELDS. Note KNOWN_PACKAGE_FIELDS does NOT contain 'target', so the '_target: &target ~/.config/bat/config' anchor documented at docs/package-files.md:797 stays legal — that scoping is load-bearing and must be preserved.

Deliberately excluded from selfie-kj5y's scope, which the bead confines to 'inside a dotfile entry'. Whether to fold it into that unit or fix separately is being decided; if selfie-n310's unit takes it, close this against that PR.
acceptance_criteria: A _-prefixed top-level key that shadows a known package field is refused by apply, not only reported by validate, while legitimate top-level anchors stay legal.
notes:
THE ONE-LINE FIX IS NOT SYMMETRIC WITH kj5y's, and that is why this must not be folded into selfie-n310's unit. Found by the plan reviewer on selfie-n310.

kj5y's fix lands in the hand-written Deserialize (package.rs:288) -> unknown_keys -> content_source() -> apply warns and skips. It reaches APPLY.

A top-level fix would land in validate_unknown_fields (validate.rs:238), which re-parses raw_yaml and is reached ONLY from Package::validate — and apply does not run validation. That is the entire premise of selfie-n310.

So the 'symmetric one-liner' would make 'selfie spec validate' report _dotfiles while 'selfie apply' continued to silently deploy nothing. Folding it into n310's unit would ship a false closure inside the one unit whose thesis is that validate-only is not enough.

Making apply catch it requires a design decision: record top-level unknown keys on Package (parallel to DotfileEntry::unknown_keys, which is what PR #71 built for entries), or the whole-package validation gate that n310's unit measured and rejected (7 test failures, including one PR #71 wrote specifically to assert the opposite shape).

ACCEPTANCE IS THEREFORE STRICTER THAN FILED: refused by APPLY, not only reported by validate.

Related: validate_unknown_fields is also inert when raw_yaml is empty or unparsable (validate.rs:229-233), so a programmatically built Package never gets top-level unknown-key diagnostics at all — see selfie-t8t2.

title: spec edit re-serializes the package before opening the editor, flattening anchors and comments
description:
crates/cli/src/commands/spec/edit.rs:63 calls common::save_package BEFORE handing the file to $EDITOR. Two consequences.

1. Every 'selfie spec edit' silently rewrites the user's YAML through serde even when they change nothing: anchors are flattened to their expanded values, comments are dropped, and key order and formatting are normalized. The user opens their editor and finds their file already altered by the act of opening it.

2. After selfie-6lz4, it is unusable on exactly the file you need it for. A package carrying an unrecognized key (e.g. 'var:' for 'vars:') is refused by the new save_package guard, so spec edit exits 1 and never opens the editor — telling the user to correct the key using the tool that just refused to let them. Recoverable by editing the YAML by hand, and refusing is strictly safer than the pre-fix behavior of silently laundering the typo, but the instruction loop is self-contradictory.

The pre-save appears to serve no purpose for an unmodified package. Likely fix: do not re-serialize before opening the editor; save only after the user's edits, or not at all if the editor writes the file in place.

Found by the final reviewer on selfie-6lz4. selfie-6lz4 makes the refusal message actionable as a stopgap; this issue is the underlying behavior.
acceptance_criteria: Opening a package with spec edit does not rewrite it, and a package with an unrecognized key can still be opened for editing.

title: A _-prefixed key that shadows a real dotfile field deploys credentials unrendered with no diagnostic
description:
selfie-6lz4 makes any _-prefixed key inside a dotfiles entry legal, so YAML anchors work. Correct and required. But it means a key that SHADOWS a real field is silently accepted.

Measured on the selfie-6lz4 branch:
  source: u/creds.tpl + _vars:   -> DEPLOYED, target contains 'api_key: {{ api_key }}' unrendered
  _source: u/plain.txt alone     -> skipped as Invalid (no real source, so refused anyway)
  source: u/plain.txt + _: 1     -> deployed (harmless)

The _vars case is the dangerous one: the bindings are silently dropped, the entry is not secret-bearing, and the template deploys with literal placeholders over a credentials target. 'selfie spec validate' on that package reported NOTHING for it — the only diagnostic was for the unrelated _source entry. So there is no signal from apply or from validate.

selfie-6lz4 documents this hazard in docs/package-files.md, which is a defensible response given the parent bead requires _ keys to be legal. But documentation is the weakest available mitigation for a silent credential failure, and the mitigation space is not empty.

Suggested direction from the final reviewer: flag a _-prefixed key whose remainder matches a KNOWN dotfile field (_vars, _source, _command, _target) as an error INSIDE a dotfile entry, while leaving all other _ keys alone. That keeps anchors working — nobody names an anchor _vars by accident — while closing the shadowing case. Consider whether the same rule should apply at the top level.

Filed so the decision is recorded rather than only documented.
acceptance_criteria: A _-prefixed key that shadows a known dotfile field produces a diagnostic, or the decision not to flag it is recorded with its reasoning.
close_reason:
Fixed in PR #75 (merged 97ff4ad).

selfie-n310: ContentSource::Invalid deleted; DotfileEntry::content_source() returns Result<ContentSource, InvalidEntry>. Both options the bead named were measured and rejected — a whole-package validation gate fails 7 tests including one asserting a bad entry is skipped WHILE the package's other dotfiles still deploy, and a ValidatedPackage type would be constructed at one internal site (apply_all takes no packages) so it is that gate wearing a type.

The claim is deliberately limited and the code says so: the compiler forces a decision at 11 of 11 consumers where 5 were forced before; it does NOT make dropping impossible, since 'let Ok(x) = ... else { continue }' still compiles. Each consumer has a regression test asserting the refusal is REPORTED, which is the guard on that residual.

The concrete hole closed: ContentSource's Display had an Invalid arm, so a malformed entry was printable as though it named a source.

selfie-3c5a: refused before any command runs. Verified by running the same test against both commits — at base the credential fetch fired ('op read op://Private/rubygems/token') and the target was written; after, zero calls and no file, across apply, drift and dry-run.

selfie-kj5y: a _-prefixed key shadowing a known dotfile field is refused. Boundaries verified against built code: _source/_command/_vars/_target refused inside an entry; _anchor, _brew, _targets, __vars and bare _ still legal; the documented TOP-LEVEL _target anchor still parses and resolves through its alias.

TWO THINGS ADDED ON MAINTAINER REVIEW, both from the same root cause — validation was gating on a deploy-path classification:
1. template_dotfiles() no longer routes through content_source(), so a bad var name no longer suppresses 'declared but never used' for other vars in the same entry. docs/package-files.md:576 already stated that rule unqualified; the code had drifted from the docs.
2. The apply-time command notice counted via command_count(), which returns 0 for a refused entry — so 'vars: { not-a-name: curl example.com | sh }' produced SILENCE from the check meant to help judge whether to trust a package. It now counts what the entry declares. command_count() is unchanged for apply's dry-run: validation asks what the file declares, apply asks what it will run, with a test pinning them to agree for every valid shape.

crates/selfie/src/package/validate.rs now contains no call to content_source() at all.

NOT closed by this: n310's motivating anecdote, a templated source escaping the package directory. That was a missing containment guard on a perfectly VALID Template; root cause is selfie-zv4b.

title: dotfiles drift reports a symlink-refused entry as 'repo changed' forever with no explanation
description:
After selfie-4m9 a dotfile whose target is a symlink is refused at apply and never deployed. 'selfie dotfiles drift' then reports it as 'repo changed' on every run, permanently, because the repo file's checksum keeps moving away from a target that is never updated.

docs/sync.md points users at 'drift' as the command for details on what is out of sync. It is therefore the one command a confused user is most likely to reach for, and it is the one command that cannot tell them the word 'symlink'. The user sees persistent drift with no cause and no remedy.

Verified by probe during selfie-4m9 implementation. Deliberately left silent in that unit because drift is a read-only command and adding a filesystem stat to it is a behavior change beyond a P1's scope — but that was a decision made in passing rather than a recorded one, which is why this exists.

Options: have drift stat the target and report 'refused: target is a symlink', or have it report the entry as blocked rather than changed.
acceptance_criteria: A dotfile refused because its target is a symlink is reported by drift with the reason, not as an unexplained permanent 'repo changed'.
notes:
CONTRADICTORY OBSERVATIONS from two agents, both plausible — resolve before fixing.

The selfie-4m9 author reported drift shows a refused entry as 'repo changed' FOREVER. The selfie-4m9 final reviewer reported the opposite: handle_check_drift (service.rs:1389) expands the target the same way but reads THROUGH the link and checksums the DESTINATION, so it reports 'in sync' for a target apply will refuse to write.

Both are reachable and neither is wrong — which one you get depends on whether the symlink destination's content happens to match the repo file. Destination matches -> 'in sync' while apply refuses. Destination differs -> 'repo changed' permanently, because the target never updates.

So the real defect is broader than first filed: drift and apply DISAGREE about what a symlinked target is, in both directions, and drift cannot say the word 'symlink' either way. Pre-existing rather than introduced by selfie-4m9 (drift already read through links), but selfie-4m9 makes it user-visible by giving apply a refusal that drift does not model.

Fix should make drift describe the target the same way apply does.
MECHANISM CORRECTED (2026-07-31), verified independently by the unit-A plan author and its reviewer with real symlinks against the real DotfileServiceImpl.

THE NOTE ABOVE IS WRONG ABOUT WHY THE TWO AGENTS DISAGREED. It says which behavior you get 'depends on whether the symlink destination's content happens to match the repo file.' The actual selector is the RECORDED DEPLOY-STATE ENTRY. record_deployment (state.rs:66-76) writes source_checksum == deployed_checksum, and detect_drift (state.rs:78-96) compares LIVE checksums against that recorded entry.

So the two reported behaviors are not two configurations -- they are TWO CONSECUTIVE POINTS ON ONE TIMELINE, separated by a single edit to the repository file. Both agents were right; each described a different moment.

Also wrong: 'destination differs -> repo changed'. A destination differing from the recorded deployed_checksum yields TargetChanged, never RepoChanged. RepoChanged requires the REPO file to move.

MEASURED, five states, none of which contains the word 'symlink':
  1a symlink, never deployed, destination DIFFERS -> drift 'not tracked' (counted, no warning); apply refuses + warns
  1b symlink, never deployed, destination MATCHES -> drift 'not tracked' (counted, no warning); apply SILENT
  2  deployed, then stow-migrated, repo unchanged  -> drift silent, drift_count=0; apply silent. THEY AGREE HERE
  3  ...then repo file edited                      -> drift 'repo changed' FOREVER (3 rounds, state file byte-identical); apply refuses every round
  4  deployed, then linked to different content    -> drift 'target changed'; apply refuses
  5  dangling symlink, never deployed              -> drift 'not tracked'

A THIRD CLASSIFICATION NEITHER AGENT REPORTED: 'not tracked' (1a, 1b, 5). This is the FRESH-MACHINE case -- new laptop, config already symlinked into place by stow/yadm/Syncthing, then selfie apply. Arguably the most common way anyone meets this bug, and it is in neither the description nor the original note.

THE ORIGINAL REVIEWER'S CLAIM OVERSHOT BY ONE STEP: reading through the link is real, but 'reports in sync for a target apply will refuse to write' is not what happens in row 2 -- apply does not WANT to write there, takes DeployDecision::Skip, and the refusal check at service.rs:1305 is deliberately excluded from Skip by a 25-line comment. Row 2 is agreement. The genuine disagreement is rows 1a, 1b, 3, 4.

Row 2 is manufactured by selfie-ywvs (now P1): track on a symlinked target silently creates exactly that state.
close_reason: Closed

title: Make the never-canonicalize-a-target rule structural instead of prose
description:
Before selfie-4m9, the no-canonicalization rule on the credential path was enforced STRUCTURALLY: two separate expanders existed (expand_user_path, which canonicalized, and expand_secret_target, which did not), and .claude/rules/secrets.md said do not merge them. A mistake in the repository-file expander physically could not reach credentials.

selfie-4m9 unifies them into one non-canonicalizing expand_target_path — which the bead required, and which is correct, because de-canonicalization turned out to be load-bearing for the repository path too. But the blast radius goes up: one function now serves both paths, and a single edit to it (someone 'fixing' the /tmp vs /private/tmp duplicate-detection regression by reaching for expand_path) reopens the hole for credentials simultaneously. The only thing standing in the way afterwards is a sentence in a rules file.

.claude/rules/testing.md states the preference directly: 'A compile error beats a test... prove it by making the violation fail to build.' .claude/rules/verification.md states it too: 'An invariant you can state is not an invariant the code enforces.'

Proposal: a TargetPath newtype constructible ONLY by the non-canonicalizing expander, with the write primitives accepting TargetPath rather than &Path. A call site that canonicalizes then writes would fail to compile. Roughly 9 call sites today (7 for the former expand_user_path, 2 for the former expand_secret_target).

Deliberately not done inside selfie-4m9 — a type refactor across every target-path call site should not ride on a P1 security fix. Confirmed with the maintainer 2026-07-29.
acceptance_criteria: A call site that canonicalizes a dotfile target path before writing fails to compile, rather than being caught only by a rules-file sentence.

title: is_secret_bearing() has no production callers — a guard that guards nothing
description:
DotfileEntry::is_secret_bearing (crates/selfie/src/package.rs:270) is public API with a name that reads as a safety predicate. Verified with 'grep -rn is_secret_bearing crates --include=*.rs': the only hits are its own definition and five assertions in package.rs tests. No production code path calls it.

So either it is dead public API, or it is a guard someone intended to call on the apply path and did not. The five tests assert it returns the right answer, which makes it look maintained and load-bearing while nothing consults it — the tests are the only consumer.

This matters more than a typical dead-code finding because of what it is named. .claude/rules/secrets.md records three leak paths found by three different reviewers and concludes 'assume there is a fourth'. A reviewer scanning for how selfie distinguishes secret-bearing entries will find this method, read its five green tests, and reasonably conclude the distinction is enforced somewhere. It is not.

Resolve by either deleting it, or finding the call site it was written for and wiring it up.

Found by the plan reviewer on selfie-6lz4.
acceptance_criteria: is_secret_bearing is either removed or called from the production path it was written to guard.
close_reason:
Fixed in PR #76 (merged). DotfileEntry::is_secret_bearing removed along with its six test assertions.

It read as a safety predicate — whether an entry's content is produced by running commands, and therefore must not enter deploy state or an event — and had green tests asserting it answered correctly. Nothing called it. Verified three ways across two units: grep, renaming it and building the workspace clean, and finally by deleting it, which is the proof that stands in the history — if anything had used it, the commit would not compile.

Deleting is an improvement rather than a subtraction. Production dispatches on 'match entry.content_source()' with exhaustive arms, which is stronger than a bool: rustc forces every variant to be handled where a predicate collapses the choice into a branch nobody has to write. The auto_accept guard secrets.md requires is enforced the same way — the secret branch returns before the flag is read — not by consulting a predicate.

Deferred out of PR #74 because it touches package.rs, which PR #75 owned.

title: pre-commit-check skill runs clippy without -D warnings, the exact trap CLAUDE.md warns about
description:
.claude/skills/pre-commit-check/SKILL.md:10 runs 'cargo clippy --all-targets' and labels it 'zero warnings policy' on the same line. That form does NOT fail on warnings.

CLAUDE.md:25 and CLAUDE.md:37 both warn about precisely this: the bare form under-reports, CI runs '-- -D warnings', and using the bare form locally ships a warning to a red build. The skill that exists to automate the pre-commit checklist runs the under-reporting form, so an agent that dutifully invokes the skill gets a green report and then a red CI.

Fix: change step 2 to 'cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings' to match CLAUDE.md's documented CI form.

Also worth checking while there: the skill omits 'dprint fmt', which is step 2 of CLAUDE.md's four-step pre-commit checklist and is enforced by 'dprint check' in CI. So the skill under-covers the checklist in two ways.

Found by the plan reviewer on selfie-4b7.
acceptance_criteria: The pre-commit-check skill runs the same clippy form CI runs, and covers every step of the CLAUDE.md pre-commit checklist.
notes:
RESOLUTION CHANGED 2026-07-29 by the maintainer. The skill is being DELETED, not corrected.

Reasoning, which is the same insight the fix itself was built on: the skill duplicated a checklist already present in CLAUDE.md and already loaded every session. That duplication is what produced this bug. Correcting the skill's commands (or delegating them to the Justfile) fixes the instance and leaves the mechanism; deleting the skill removes the second copy entirely.

CLAUDE.md's pre-commit checklist is being rewritten to delegate to 'just check' plus 'just test-lib' (settling selfie-it6l), to state that passing is not the same as CI being green, and to record the maintainer's formatting policy. selfie-cm1h is folded into the same edit.

Acceptance is therefore satisfied differently than filed: the skill cannot run the wrong clippy form because the skill no longer exists.

Fixed in PR #73 (merged d9bb7f9).

It duplicated a checklist CLAUDE.md already carries and already loads every session, and that duplication is what let the two drift apart. CLAUDE.md's checklist now delegates to 'just check', so no second copy of the commands exists to weaken. Premise verified empirically rather than restated: on an isolated copy with a planted clippy::needless_return, 'cargo clippy --all-targets' exits 0 while printing the warning and '-- -D warnings' exits 101 on identical code.

The question assumed a hand-picked crate+feature invocation was the right instrument. selfie is the only crate in the workspace with an optional feature (with_mocks; mockall is the only optional=true dependency), so it was the only crate worth isolating and nothing said why. CI now runs 'cargo hack --each-feature test -p selfie', covering all four combinations instead of the one the workspace run produces, and extending itself if a second feature appears. title: A corrupt deploy-state file is silently swallowed, turning routine applies into conflicts
description:
load_deploy_state (crates/selfie/src/dotfile_service/service.rs:217) ends in unwrap_or_else(|_| DeployState::empty()). An unparseable or truncated state file is therefore replaced by an empty one with no error, no warning, and no event.

Consequence: every tracked dotfile suddenly looks NotTracked. Routine applies that would have been quiet Skip-or-update decisions become conflicts, and the user is prompted about files selfie has managed for months with no indication that the state file is the reason. Answering those prompts then overwrites the state with a fresh empty-derived one, destroying whatever was recoverable.

Silent fallback on corrupt persistent state is the failure mode selfie-hat records the user's principle about: selfie must not fail silently — if it can proceed, it should, but it must say what it ignored.

Should emit a warning event naming the state file and the parse error, and consider preserving the corrupt file rather than overwriting it.

Found while planning selfie-4m9.
acceptance_criteria: A deploy-state file that fails to parse produces a warning event naming the file, rather than being silently replaced by an empty state.

title: DeployEntry::target is recorded but never read, so a changed target orphans the old file
description:
record_deployment stores DeployEntry::target in the deploy state, but nothing ever reads it for a decision — DeployState::detect_drift keys on source alone.

Consequence: if a package's 'target:' is edited, the state entry keyed by the unchanged source still matches. Drift is then computed against the NEW target while the OLD target file is left on disk, silently orphaned, with no event telling the user a file was abandoned. selfie no longer manages it and never mentions it again.

Either use the stored target to detect that the configured target moved (and emit an event, or clean up), or drop the field so the state file does not carry data that implies a guarantee it does not provide.

Found while planning selfie-4m9. Note that selfie-4m9 changes the recorded target string from a canonicalized path to the as-configured path; that change is only safe BECAUSE the field is never read, which is exactly the coupling this issue is about.
acceptance_criteria: Either a changed target is detected and reported using the recorded value, or the unused field is removed.

title: EnvironmentConfig has no unknown-field detection
description:
Unknown keys inside an environments.<env> block are silently dropped. Verified empirically: 'environments.test.instal: typo' (for 'install') parses clean and produces ZERO validation issues.

'install' is required, so a bare misspelling of it is caught by serde's 'missing field' error. But 'chekc:' for 'check:', 'dependancies:' for 'dependencies:', and 'recomends:' are all silently ignored — the user gets no signal that the key did nothing.

Same class of bug as selfie-6lz4, one level down. validate_unknown_fields (crates/selfie/src/package/validate.rs:195) already walks top-level keys and, after selfie-6lz4, walks dotfiles entries; extending it to EnvironmentConfig fields is the same shape of change plus a KNOWN_ENVIRONMENT_FIELDS const.

Found while planning selfie-6lz4; deliberately left out of that unit's scope.
acceptance_criteria: An unknown key inside an environments block produces a field-level validation error naming the environment and the key.

title: An invalid var name still runs its command and deploys the file unrendered
description:

What happens instead: content_source() returns Template because it only tests vars.is_empty(), so the entry is secret-bearing and reaches SecretApply. resolve_content runs 'op read x', a real credential fetch that can raise a biometric or password prompt, and inserts the value into bindings. template::render then rejects the name at is_valid_name and copies the placeholder verbatim. The file deploys through write_file_private with a literal {{ not-a-name }} where the credential belongs.

So a command executes for a binding that provably cannot be substituted, the value is fetched and discarded, and a malformed credentials file is written. Related to but distinct from apply not gating on validation generally: here the entry is known unusable before any command runs, and check_resolvable already exists as the place to refuse things decidable without executing anything.

The doc comment on template::is_valid_name says the shared name check means validation 'rejects illegal names before apply', which is what the apply path does not do.
acceptance_criteria: An entry whose var name cannot be substituted is refused before any command runs.

title: ADR-0003 claims the no-leak rule is structurally enforced; it is call-site discipline
description:
docs/adr/0003-no-deploy-state-for-provider-sourced-dotfiles.md:53 states: 'Because the event stream is the library's only unconditional egress, this is enforced where events are constructed rather than at each call site.'

The actual enforcement is entirely at the call sites in dotfile_service/service.rs, where secret_origin and secret_conflict_summary build safe strings and each SecretApply phase is individually careful.
