title: CLI apply runs provider commands under /bin/sh while install and MCP use a login shell
description:
Commit 31bf6bc established login-shell execution for the MCP server and 9e918a7 did the same for the CLI, so the user's profile and PATH are available during install, check and audit. The MCP half of provider-sourced dotfiles inherited it (crates/mcp-server/src/server.rs:228, with a comment noting that op and teller live on the user's PATH). The CLI half did not: crates/cli/src/commands/apply.rs:221 uses ShellCommandRunner::default_shell().

default_shell() is /bin/sh on Unix, while install and check run under the user's shell with -l. Two consequences. Provider commands do not get the login profile, so anything the profile sets rather than exports — SSH_AUTH_SOCK, OP_ variables, PATH entries — is missing. And a command written in fish or zsh syntax works in 'selfie package install' and fails in 'selfie apply', while the same package behaves differently through the CLI and the MCP server.

docs/package-files.md says only that provider commands 'run through a shell', which does not distinguish them.
acceptance_criteria: A provider command sees the same shell and environment through CLI apply as it does through install and through the MCP server, or the difference is documented.
close_reason: Closed

title: Ctrl+C cannot cancel a provider command during selfie apply
description:
Commit 568c528 threaded a CancellationToken from the CLI signal handler through the service and runner layers so Ctrl+C kills in-flight subprocesses, adding a token parameter to every CommandRunner method.

The dotfile apply path does not participate. SecretApply::resolve (crates/selfie/src/dotfile_service/service.rs:705) passes &CancellationToken::new() — a fresh token nothing holds. DotfileServiceImpl::new takes no token, unlike PackageServiceImpl::new. And crates/cli/src/commands.rs never passes the token to handle_apply, though the Spec and Package arms beside it do.

Harmless before this feature, because apply executed nothing. Now Ctrl+C during 'selfie apply' cannot kill an 'op read' blocked on a biometric or password prompt; command_timeout still bounds it, so it is not unbounded, but the interactive escape hatch 568c528 exists to provide is absent and no cancellation event is emitted.
acceptance_criteria: Ctrl+C during selfie apply cancels an in-flight provider command, as it does during install and check.
close_reason: Closed

title: Deploy state file is written world-readable
description:
save_deploy_state (crates/selfie/src/dotfile_service/service.rs:232) writes ~/.local/state/selfie/deploy-state.yml with FileSystem::write_file, so it lands at the process umask default, typically 0644. Secret-bearing dotfile targets are written owner-only at 0600, which makes the state file the weaker of the two.

Its contents are not credentials, but they are a complete map of every target path selfie manages on the machine, plus checksums of repository files. That is a reconnaissance aid on a shared host, and it is readable by anyone when the things it describes are not.

FileSystem::write_file_private already exists and does exactly what is needed — owner-only at creation, atomic replace. The change is the call site plus a test asserting the mode.

This also underpins ADR-0003's refusal to store checksums of secrets. That argument turns on the state file being easier to read than the secret itself; make the file owner-only and the asymmetry disappears, which is a precondition for selfie-0ei5 to even be worth considering.
acceptance_criteria: The deploy state file is readable only by its owner, with a test asserting it.

The umask-vacuity guard panics when CI is set and skips only locally, so it cannot silently prove nothing on a runner (CI is ubuntu-latest, default umask 022, so it does not fire there).

description:

Simple and closes it outright, but it is a behavior change: packages that apply today would stop, including ones whose only defect is unrelated to the entry being deployed. Needs a decision about partial application and about which validation levels block.

Or make the invalid state unrepresentable where it is consumed — have apply take a type that can only be constructed from a validated package, so a consumer cannot reach an entry without having refused the invalid case. That converts a rule everyone must remember into a compile error, which is the form that actually holds. Larger change, and it is the direction this codebase has repeatedly found to be the one that sticks.

title: Allow a dotfile entry to specify the deployed file mode
description:
A dotfile entry cannot say what permissions its target should have. Repository-file entries land at the process umask default, typically 0644, and only secret-bearing entries get 0600, automatically and inexpressibly.

A group- or world-readable mode on a secret-bearing entry should be a validation error, not a warning — the same reasoning that made auto_accept not apply to those entries.

title: cargo test -p selfie does not compile without --features with_mocks
description:
CLAUDE.md documents 'cargo test -p selfie   # Test library only' as a working command, but it fails to compile with unresolved imports for MockFileSystem, MockPackageRepository, MockCommandRunner and others — the mocks are gated behind the with_mocks feature.

It appears to work only because a workspace-wide 'cargo test' unifies the feature in from selfie-cli's dev-dependencies, so the failure is invisible unless the crate is tested alone. Reproduced on a clean tree, so it is pre-existing and unrelated to any current feature work.

Fix by either enabling with_mocks for the crate's own test builds or correcting the documented command in CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md.
acceptance_criteria: The command documented in CLAUDE.md for testing the library alone actually compiles and runs.
close_reason:
Fixed in PR #70 (merged 19caf87). The compile failure was real when filed and was fixed incidentally by PR #67, which added features=[with_mocks] to test-common's dependency on selfie; test-common is a dev-dependency of selfie, so Cargo unifies the feature into selfie's own test build. What remained broken was CLAUDE.md, which documented the fixed trap as current fact and prescribed an unnecessary flag, contradicting Justfile:31. PR #70 corrects CLAUDE.md and architecture.md, and adds a CI step running the library crate alone, since every workspace-wide command unifies the feature in and so cannot catch this class of break.

NOTE: this bead's acceptance criteria named AGENTS.md, which no longer exists - deleted in cf1efe9 the same day this bead was filed. Only CLAUDE.md needed correcting.

title: Validate environment-specific dotfiles + surface overrides in spec validation

title: Secret provider integration point for dotfiles (shell out to 1Password/teller, don't reinvent)

Fits selfie's command-runner identity. DotfileEntry content source becomes: repo file (source) OR provider command (secret/from ref). At apply, run the provider, write result to target; never commit or persist the secret value; drift/state must NOT store the secret's checksum/value (needs distinct semantics - part of this design). Use case: private RubyGems server creds on work machine. User standardizes on 1Password (personal+work) and teller (work GCP/dotenv). title: Dotfiles are single-source, not per-environment — no machine-specific config variants (YADM alt-file parity)

YADM handles this via alt-files (##os.Linux, ##hostname) and templates. For selfie's home+work cross-machine goal this is a structural gap: today the user must unify configs across machines or they'll conflict on deploy. Options to design: per-environment dotfile overrides/variants, templating, or an explicit 'shared vs machine-specific' split. Relates to selfie-522 (environment inheritance). Surfaced 2026-07-23.
design: Per-environment dotfiles (ADR-0001, Problem A). Add optional 'dotfiles: Vec<DotfileEntry>' to EnvironmentConfig. Effective set for current env = top-level shared dotfiles, with any entry whose resolved target matches an env-specific entry REPLACED by it, unioned with env-specific entries introducing new targets. Env-specific overrides shared keyed on target; otherwise added (presence). No exclusion (YAGNI). Source resolution unchanged (relative to package YAML dir). git identity is out of scope (use git-native includeIf). DotfileEntry to gain a content-source abstraction so it composes with secret providers (selfie-B). No backward compat (pre-release).

title: Show dependency satisfaction status in package info
description:

title: Show git-dirty indicator on package info commands
description:
Commands that display package information (info, list, check, validate, audit) should also indicate whether the local package YAML file has uncommitted git changes. This helps users notice when their package specs have been modified locally but not yet committed, which matters for keeping configs in sync across machines.

Scope: Add a git-status indicator (e.g., 'modified', 'untracked', 'staged') to package output in commands that report package details. The indicator should appear alongside existing package metadata.

Implementation considerations:
- The selfie library has no git functionality today — this is net-new.
- Following hexagonal architecture, git operations should go behind a trait/port (e.g., GitStatusProvider) so the CLI can use a real implementation and tests can mock it.
- The library should emit git status info via PackageEvent so each frontend (CLI, MCP) can render it appropriately.
- Need to handle: file is untracked, file has staged changes, file has unstaged changes. Also handle gracefully when the package directory is not a git repo.
- Skip unpushed detection — committed is sufficient. This avoids complexity around missing upstream tracking branches.
- Performance: for the list command, checking git status for many files should be efficient (e.g., one 'git status --porcelain' call for the whole directory, not one per file).

Remove async-trait crate; use Rust's native async fn in traits (stable since 1.75). Upgrade mockall from 0.13.1 to 0.14.0 which supports native async trait mocking.

Files using #[async_trait]: commands/runner.rs, commands/shell.rs, package/service.rs (×2), config/loader.rs. Note: ConfigLoader uses #[async_trait] but has no async methods — can just remove it.

Mocked async traits: CommandRunner (4 async methods), PackageService (7 async methods). Both use #[automock] + #[async_trait] together.

Benefit: Removes heap allocation per async trait call, removes a dependency, uses idiomatic modern Rust.

Risk: mockall 0.14.0 is a major version bump — may have breaking API changes beyond async trait support. Run full test suite after upgrade.
close_reason: Removed async-trait, upgraded mockall to 0.14, native RPITIT async traits, fixed mock visibility and hardcoded shell path

title: OperationFailure duplicates PackageError types field-for-field
description: OperationFailure has variants like PackageFailure::NotFound that mirror PackageError::PackageNotFound field-for-field, creating a parallel error hierarchy. When an error occurs, the same information exists in both PackageError and OperationFailure. OperationFailure should reference or wrap PackageError rather than duplicating its structure. Related to selfie-mqq (double event emission).
close_reason: Merged EnvironmentFailure and PackageFailure enums into OperationFailure::Package(PackageError) wrapper. Deleted ~130 lines of duplicate type definitions and field-copying conversion code.

title: Implement PackageService::create or remove from trait
description: PackageService::create is declared in the trait but the implementation is a stub that returns a placeholder success. The CLI's create.rs bypasses the service entirely and uses PackageRepository directly — the most significant hexagonal architecture boundary violation. Either implement create properly in the service (with event streaming, validation, etc.) or remove it from the trait until ready.
close_reason: PackageService::create is now fully implemented with service handler, event variants, and CLI integration

title: Add tests for ConfigLoader and YamlLoader
description: config/loader.rs (ConfigLoader trait, ConfigLoadError) and config/yaml.rs (YamlLoader) have zero tests. This is the component responsible for finding and reading the config file on disk — a critical path with several error variants (NotFound, MultipleFound, ConfigError) that are never exercised in isolation. config/validate.rs also lacks unit tests (only tested through CLI integration tests).
close_reason: Added 10 tests covering all validation paths in config/validate.rs

title: Fix double event emission for errors
description: When an error occurs, the library emits it twice: once as PackageEvent::Error and again inside PackageEvent::Completed { result: Failure } with a re-serialized copy in OperationFailure. This forces the CLI to implement PackageNotFoundTracker as a suppression workaround in common.rs. The Completed event should reference the error, not duplicate it. Additionally, OperationFailure duplicates error types field-for-field (e.g., PackageFailure::NotFound mirrors PackageError::PackageNotFound).
close_reason: Fixed in db33934: eliminated double event emission and removed PackageNotFoundTracker workaround

title: Unify PackageService return types across all methods
description: PackageService methods have inconsistent return types: check/install return EventStream directly, while info/validate/list return Result<EventStream, PackageError>. All methods should use the same pattern. Either all return EventStream (encoding early-exit errors as the first event in the stream) or all return Result<EventStream>. The inconsistency forces callers to handle two different patterns.
close_reason: Already fixed in commits 1cbab63, db33934, 9ca8c98, d9ce8a1. All six PackageService methods now uniformly return EventStream directly.

title: CLI commands should accept Box<dyn PackageService> for testability
description: CLI command handlers use the concrete type PackageServiceImpl<YamlPackageRepository<RealFileSystem>, ShellCommandRunner> via create_package_service() in common.rs. This prevents injecting MockPackageService for unit testing. Commands should accept Box<dyn PackageService> (dynamic dispatch) so mock services can be used in tests. MockPackageService and MockCommandRunner are defined but never used because of this.
close_reason: Refactored all 6 CLI command handlers to accept &dyn PackageService parameter instead of creating service internally. Service creation now happens at the dispatch_package_command level in commands.rs.

title: Fix event_processor tests using real filesystem
description: event_processor.rs tests (lines 328-418) create real ShellCommandRunner and RealFileSystem instances pointing at /tmp/nonexistent. These tests depend on filesystem state and could behave differently in CI. Replace with mock-based tests for deterministic behavior.
close_reason: Already fixed: tests now use stream::iter(vec![...]) to construct EventStream directly, with no real filesystem or command runner dependencies.

title: Audit console/dialoguer in library crate dependencies
description: The console and dialoguer crates are listed as dependencies of the selfie library crate (Cargo.toml). These are terminal UI crates that don't appear to be used in the library's production code. Verify usage and move to [dev-dependencies] or remove entirely -- these belong only in the CLI crate.
close_reason: Removed unused console dependency from selfie library Cargo.toml

title: Encapsulate GetPackage fields
description: GetPackage has pub fields (package, file_path, is_new) rather than accessor methods. The CLI's create.rs constructs GetPackage directly, bypassing any encapsulation. Make fields pub(crate) and provide public constructors/accessors, similar to how Package is already designed. This is API hygiene for v1.
close_reason: Encapsulated GetPackage fields and implemented PackageService::create

title: Eliminate the capture-descriptor collision class rather than narrowing it
description:
selfie-evf9's fix captures a provider command's stdout on a fixed file descriptor (8) so a login profile's own output cannot be spliced into a deployed credential. A profile that takes descriptor 8 -- 'exec 8>somewhere' -- receives the content instead, and selfie then fails closed with nothing deployed.

That residual is DOCUMENTED, not defended, and deliberately so: the threat model is ACCIDENTAL collision, not an adversarial startup file. A hostile profile already owns the session -- it can read the deployed credential directly or wrap 'op' -- so the capture descriptor is not a security boundary. Filing the elimination option so 'we chose to narrow it' is a recorded decision with a named alternative.

WHY A FIXED DESCRIPTOR RATHER THAN A RANDOM ONE, since that reasoning should survive:
- A fixed number can be NAMED in the documentation and acted on ('selfie captures on descriptor 8; if your profile has taken it, take it back'). 'A descriptor chosen afresh each run' tells the user nothing.
- A collision on a fixed descriptor fails EVERY apply, so the user investigates and the leak stops. A collision on a random one over five values gives four successes in five, so the user retries the odd failure and keeps leaking one credential copy in five, indefinitely.
- 8 specifically: 3 and 4 are the conventional first-free descriptors; flock's convention is 'exec 9>lockfile'. That leaves 5-8, and 8 is furthest from the claimed ones.
- The range is 5-9 and not higher because dash, zsh and ksh all REJECT a redirect to descriptor 10 or above. Measured at 3, 9, 19, 47, 63, 90; only bash and fish accept the high ones, and the outer wrapper is /bin/sh, which is dash on Linux CI.

THE ELIMINATION OPTION, evaluated and deferred: path-based capture through a FIFO in a private 0700 directory. It removes the numbered-descriptor class entirely. Costs measured before deferring:
- reintroduces unsafe (the current design has none) for libc::mkfifo -- though note libc is ALREADY a cfg(unix) dependency of selfie, so no new crate;
- tokio's 'net' feature is not enabled, so a non-blocking FIFO reader needs that feature or a hand-rolled O_NONBLOCK + AsyncFd;
- THE DECIDING COST: the failure mode changes shape. Today a profile that exits before the recipe runs fails in milliseconds. With a read-only FIFO and no writer, the read stalls to command_timeout -- sixty seconds by default, on the credential path, for EVERY user rather than the few with a collision. Trading a rare deterministic failure for a common slow one is the wrong direction for a P1.

ALSO RECORDED, so nobody re-derives it: the cheap hardening -- have the recipe check '[ -p /dev/fd/8 ]' and refuse before writing, so a collision leaks nothing -- DOES NOT WORK. On macOS that test is false even for a genuine pipe, in all five POSIX shells, because /dev/fd entries stat as character devices there. The guard would refuse every run on macOS.

If this is taken up, do it on its own rather than gating the P1 on new failure modes.
notes:
REFRAMING, verified independently on main (2026-07-31). Earlier discussion of this work described the capture descriptor as a NEW credential egress created by the fix. That was wrong, and the reviewer withdrew it after measuring main directly.

A login profile containing 'exec >$HOME/stolen.log' -- redirecting the shell's STDOUT -- already receives the credential verbatim on today's main, with selfie's capture left empty. Measured on all five POSIX shells:

  sh, dash, bash, zsh, ksh:  capture=[]  stolen.log=SECRET1234

And 'exec >somewhere' is a considerably more common idiom than 'exec 8>somewhere'.

So selfie-evf9's wrapper NARROWS a pre-existing class rather than creating one: it moves the content off the shell's stdout -- the descriptor profiles actually redirect -- onto an uncommon numbered one. Measured against the same profile, the wrapped run captures the content intact and stolen.log stays empty.

This bead is therefore about ELIMINATING a residual that predates the fix and was reduced by it, not about closing a hole the fix opened. The distinction matters for prioritisation: nothing regressed.

title: Async profile output survives the stdout fence
description:
Filed as the known residual of selfie-evf9's fix, so the gap is recorded rather than implied.

The stdout fence being built for selfie-evf9 is TIME-ORDERED, not source-separated: it discards bytes written before the command's first byte. A login profile that BACKGROUNDS a writer holding fd 1 therefore splices inside the fence.

Measured with a profile doing '{ sleep 0.2; printf ASYNCCHATTER; } &' -- the shape of async update-checkers and version-manager notices -- in all five POSIX shells tested:

  sh dash bash zsh ksh  ->  EXTRACT[[ASYNCCHATTERs3cr3t-Value-9x7]]

AND IT IS A RACE, not a constant. With the command sleeping 0 / 0.1 / 0.4s the results were clean, clean, spliced. A real 'op read' takes several hundred ms, so the window is wide. That also means it will reproduce intermittently and look like flakiness rather than a bug.

THE FIX IS KNOWN AND WAS MEASURED IMMUNE: file-descriptor separation at spawn time -- child gets fd1 = /dev/null and fd3 = the capture pipe, command output redirected to fd3. A backgrounded child inherits fd1 = /dev/null and never touches the capture fd. Verified immune in all five shells.

WHY IT WAS NOT DONE IN selfie-evf9: it requires one unsafe { pre_exec } dup2 (tokio's Command reaches pre_exec only via as_std_mut), and it loses the discarded-byte count that drives that unit's warning unless fd1 becomes a second counting pipe. No no-unsafe variant was found: doing 'exec 3>&1 1>/dev/null' inside the -c string is too late, because the profile's background children already hold the real pipe.

Note the two mechanisms are COMPLEMENTARY, not alternatives: the fence covers zsh/ksh trailing exit-trap output that fd separation leaks into the capture fd, and fd separation covers the async case the fence cannot see. A complete fix is both.

Found by the selfie-evf9 plan reviewer.
close_reason: Closed

title: sync status drops Warning events, so it cannot relay a drift reason
description:
crates/selfie/src/sync_service/service.rs:910-943, collect_drift_summary matches only DotfileDriftDetected and Completed; every other event hits '_ => {}'. Warning events are discarded.

Consequence after unit A of the target-semantics batch lands: 'selfie dotfiles drift' will name a symlinked target as the reason an entry is stuck, but 'selfie sync status' -- which reads the same stream -- will still say '1 drifted' with no mention of why. And docs/sync.md points the user at drift for the details, so the two commands disagree about how much they know.

That is acceptable as a division of labor (the summary points at the detailed command, and the detailed command answers), which is why unit A scoped it out rather than widening the SyncStatus event shape mid-unit. Filing so the gap is a recorded decision rather than an oversight.

Fix direction: decide whether the drift summary should carry a reason at all. If yes, it needs a field on the summary rather than free text, since the MCP server serializes it -- and adding a Warning passthrough would put arbitrary library text into a structured surface, which .claude/rules/architecture.md argues against. Consider instead a typed 'blocked' count alongside 'drifted'.

Found by the unit-A plan author and confirmed by its reviewer.

title: Record the non-racy option for the lexical containment guard
description:
selfie-86o was resolved by DOCUMENTING that is_within is lexical rather than by fixing it, which is the branch that bead's own either/or criteria permits and that .claude/rules/secrets.md:158 instructs. Filing the alternative so 'we chose to document' is a recorded decision with a named option rather than an absence.

THE OPTION: a FileSystem::read_within(base, relative) port method backed by cap-std or openat2's RESOLVE_BENEATH. Kernel-enforced containment, so it is NOT the check-then-read TOCTOU race that a userspace symlink walk would be -- which matters, because selfie-4m9 spent a P1 closing exactly that class using O_NOFOLLOW, and adding a racy check that ADVERTISES symlink protection would replace an honestly-lexical guard with a dishonestly-strong one.

It is also the correct hexagonal shape: paths.rs imports only std::path and has no FileSystem, which is the whole reason it cannot do this today. A port method threaded through the four is_within call sites (service.rs:1212, service.rs:1535, resolve.rs:100, yaml.rs:142) keeps the boundary intact, and CLAUDE.md's 'lean towards third-party libraries for substantial features' argues for the crate rather than a hand-rolled walk.

WHY IT WAS DEFERRED, not rejected: selfie-86o is a P3 whose threat model requires a hostile package repository, and resolve.rs already observes that such a repository can simply run an arbitrary command: -- so this guard is not the security boundary in that scenario. The cost (a new port method, four call sites, a new dependency) is disproportionate to that.

WHEN IT WOULD BECOME WORTH DOING: if selfie ever gains a path where a package repository is not fully trusted -- shared/team package directories, a package registry, or anything fetched rather than authored locally. At that point the lexical guard's documented limit stops being acceptable and this is the fix to reach for.

Verify cap-std / openat2 guarantees against their source and check macOS support before adopting -- .claude/rules/verification.md records three claims about a crate's behavior that were wrong in this repo, one in the unsafe direction. RESOLVE_BENEATH is Linux-specific; cap-std's macOS story needs checking.

Raised by the unit-A plan reviewer.
notes: CORRECTION (2026-07-31): the note above says cap-std and openat2 RESOLVE_BENEATH are both 'kernel-enforced'. That is only true of openat2, which is Linux-only. cap-std is kernel-enforced WHERE openat2 is available; elsewhere -- macOS included -- it emulates resolution in userspace, so the race-freedom property does not carry over. Since this project's developer is on macOS and CI is Ubuntu, a cap-std-based fix would be TOCTOU-free in CI and racy locally, which is the worst configuration for noticing. Verify against cap-std's source before adopting, and if the guarantee matters, say 'kernel-enforced on Linux' rather than 'kernel-enforced'.

title: Reconsider try_send vs send().await for streamed chunks once the pump is async
description:
Filed as input to selfie-qd3r / selfie-z6cr, not as a duplicate of them.

The reason execute_streaming uses a non-blocking try_send (and therefore drops chunks) is structural: handle_chunked_read_result_streaming is a SYNC fn and cannot .await a send. Commit 9891f05 replaced an earlier blocking send().await for that reason, and CommandError::Callback -- the variant that used to report the drop -- was orphaned and later deleted in PR #79.

selfie-6bav's rewrite makes the pump an async block under an outer deadline, which removes that structural constraint. The 6bav plan reviewer measured send().await in the new shape:

  RV-1a send().await: total=8 received=4 completed=true in 11.2ms

No hang, every chunk delivered, bounded by the outer timeout. So the objection that killed the blocking send in 9891f05 -- that it can stall the output pump forever on a slow consumer -- no longer applies once the pump itself is bounded.

NOT YET ESTABLISHED: the reviewer did not test it under the 8000-chunk fixture with a 50ms-per-item consumer, which by construction would take ~400s. So the open question is the resulting SLOWDOWN, not the safety. A command producing a lot of output with a slow event sink would now be throttled by the sink rather than dropping output -- which is arguably correct, and arguably a regression in perceived responsiveness.

WHY THIS MATTERS FOR qd3r: that bead's 'cheapest first' option is a drop counter plus an end-of-stream event. That was the right call while send().await could hang. It may no longer be cheapest once 6bav lands -- 'stop dropping' may be simpler than 'count the drops and report them', and it needs no new PackageEvent variant. Decide between them with the measurement, after 6bav.

title: A timed-out command leaks grandchildren that inherited its pipes
description:
When a command times out or is cancelled, ShellCommandRunner calls child.kill(). That kills only the DIRECT child. A grandchild the child spawned -- 'sh -c "daemon &"' is the ordinary shape -- survives.

MEASURED (U2's prototype, experiment E3b): after the timeout fired,
  direct child = <gone>
  grandchild sleep still running? true

So selfie can leave orphaned processes behind on every timed-out or cancelled command. They keep whatever file descriptors they inherited, including the pipes selfie was reading.

DISTINCT FROM selfie-b7mv, which is about selfie itself HANGING because a grandchild holds the pipe open past the deadline. That one closes for free under selfie-6bav's rewrite (reads and wait become one future under one deadline; measured Err(Timeout) at 2.0029s versus an 8.0089s unbounded hang today). THIS bead is the other half: even once selfie stops waiting, the grandchild is still running.

FIX DIRECTION: process-group management, so a kill reaches the whole tree. The candidate is process-wrap (watchexec org) -- U2's author checked its health rather than its reputation: version 9.1.0, published 2026-03-08, ~4.19M recent downloads. command-group is superseded (last release 2023-11-18).

DELIBERATELY NOT DONE IN selfie-6bav. Adopting a new dependency to fix an unfiled issue, inside a unit whose stated job is REMOVING hand-rolled code, would be exactly the silent scope absorption that unit was told to avoid. Filed so the decision is made on its own merits.

Verify process-wrap's actual guarantees on macOS AND Linux against its source before adopting -- .claude/rules/verification.md records three claims about a crate's behavior that were wrong here, one in the unsafe direction.

title: run_git's success path returns git stdout raw while its failure path is now type-enforced
description:
After selfie-cvpm, crates/selfie/src/git/adapter.rs's FAILURE path is compiler-enforced: GitSyncError::OperationFailed's fields are a GitMessage newtype whose only constructors redact-then-bound, so no struct-variant literal anywhere can put raw text in.

The SUCCESS path at adapter.rs:89 is not:

  Ok(String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stdout).trim().to_string())

Raw, unbounded, unredacted.

NOT A LEAK TODAY, verified: no current call site can echo a URL. 'remote' lists names only; rev-parse, ls-files --deleted, diff --name-status and rev-list --count cannot carry one.

The problem is the asymmetry. One half of the same function is enforced by the type system and the other half is convention, which makes the guarantee look more general than it is. A future run_git(root, &['config', '--get', 'remote.origin.url']) or ['remote', '-v'] -- both ordinary things to add -- puts a credential straight into a String return value with nothing stopping it, and the next reader has every reason to assume run_git is safe because its error path visibly is.

This is the same argument selfie-cvpm's author used to justify typing the 'operation' field even though it was not an exposure at the time: the cost is small, and the alternative is a puzzle every future reader has to re-solve.

Fix direction: return GitMessage (or a sibling type) from run_git's success path too, or document at the function why the two halves differ. Prefer the type.

Found by the selfie-cvpm final code reviewer (U4 of the command-execution batch).

title: stop_on_error governs only secret-resolution failures, which is undocumented
description:
In dotfile_service/service.rs's handle_apply, a repository-file failure always continues to the next entry, while a secret-resolution failure honors stop_on_error. The code comments this explicitly around service.rs:1046 -- so it is deliberate, not an oversight.

But stop_on_error is a user-facing config key documented as an execution setting (see .claude/rules/domain.md, docs/configuration.md), and nothing tells the user it applies to only one class of dotfile failure. Someone who sets stop_on_error: true expecting apply to halt on the first problem gets that behavior for provider/vars entries and silently does not for plain source-file entries.

Either behavior is defensible. The gap is that the config key claims more than it does, which is the same shape as the invariant-you-state-versus-invariant-you-enforce rule in .claude/rules/verification.md.

Fix direction: decide whether the asymmetry is intended. If yes, document it in docs/configuration.md and docs/package-files.md and name the reasoning. If no, make repo-file failures honor the flag too. Do not resolve it by making the doc vaguer.

Found by the selfie-w8gd/selfie-fbwo plan reviewer (U3 of the command-execution batch).

title: login_shell assumes $SHELL accepts -l -c
description:
ShellCommandRunner::login_shell (commands/shell.rs:77-92) reads $SHELL and build_command (:98-102) invokes it as '<shell> -l -c <command>'.

That contract is not universal. fish honors both -l and -c. nushell wants --login rather than -l. Other shells a user may legitimately set as $SHELL (elvish, xonsh, oil) vary. When the flags are not understood the failure is opaque -- the shell errors on its own argument parsing, so the diagnostic is about a flag the user never wrote, for a command they did write.

Pre-existing for install/check/audit and for the MCP server. selfie-w8gd extends it to CLI apply, so a user with an exotic $SHELL who could previously run 'selfie apply' under /bin/sh may find it stops working -- the fix for one bug surfacing this one.

There is a fallback but it does not cover this: login_shell falls back to default_shell() only when $SHELL is UNSET, not when it is set to something that rejects -l -c.

Fix direction: a small known-shell table mapping the login flag per shell basename (fish/bash/zsh/sh -> -l, nu -> --login), falling back to no login flag rather than to an unsupported one, so an unknown shell degrades to a working non-login invocation instead of failing. Alternatively detect the failure and re-run without -l once, though that doubles the command on the credential path and is worse.

Found by the selfie-w8gd/selfie-fbwo plan reviewer (U3 of the command-execution batch).

title: Nothing observes the reader-task abort on run_buffered's early-return arms
description:
run_buffered's timeout, cancellation and wait-failure arms call stdout_handle.abort() / stderr_handle.abort() before returning. Removing BOTH calls fails no test in the workspace -- confirmed by mutation M8 during selfie-ql8m (PR for U1 of the command-execution batch), run one-per-invocation in an isolated git archive copy.

The behavior is correct and should stay: dropping a JoinHandle merely detaches the task, so without the abort a detached reader keeps buffering a killed command's output after the caller has given up -- and on the credential path that means it keeps buffering credential bytes nobody will ever read. child.kill() only kills the direct child, so where a grandchild holds the pipe (see selfie-b7mv) the detached reader can live indefinitely.

But it is currently unenforced. A future edit can delete both aborts and every gate stays green.

Reported rather than papered over: per .claude/rules/testing.md, 'mutations that pass are informative' and the author declined to invent an observation just to make the mutation bite. Filing so the gap is tracked rather than lost.

Fix direction: find an observation that is honest rather than contrived -- e.g. assert the reader task is finished (JoinHandle::is_finished) shortly after a timeout return, or restructure so the abort is not separable from the return. If no honest observation exists, closing this as won't-fix with that reasoning recorded is a legitimate outcome.

Note the interaction with selfie-b7mv: whoever bounds the post-wait join may make this observable as a side effect.

title: push's rejection remap discards the original error wholesale
description:
crates/selfie/src/git/adapter.rs:458-466. On a failed push, the code string-matches the message for 'rejected' and substitutes a fixed diagnosis:

  'Remote has new commits. Run selfie sync pull first.'

The original error is discarded, not wrapped. A push can be rejected for reasons that are not a non-fast-forward -- a pre-receive hook rejecting the push, a protected-branch policy, a quota or file-size limit, a permission failure that git words as a rejection. All of them get told to run 'selfie sync pull', which will not help and sends the user down the wrong path with the actual reason gone.

Fix direction: keep the specific guidance for the non-fast-forward case but narrow the match, and preserve the original message either way rather than replacing it. Note the interaction with selfie-cvpm: after that lands the message is redacted and bounded, so preserving it is safe to surface -- but bounding could in principle elide the marker this match depends on when stderr is large, which is a second reason not to hinge the whole diagnosis on a substring.

Found by the selfie-cvpm plan reviewer (U4 of the command-execution batch).

title: SyncError::GitError is an untyped free-text carrier reaching MCP JSON
description:
crates/selfie/src/sync_service/port.rs:27 defines SyncError::GitError(String) -- an untyped free-text field that reaches an AI assistant's transcript directly via crates/mcp-server/src/server.rs:757-765, which builds json!({"status":"error","message": e.to_string()}) without going through the event stream.

It is safe today only because its sole source is a GitSyncError's Display. Once selfie-cvpm lands and GitSyncError's fields are a redacting type, that safety becomes a CONVENTION rather than a type: SyncError::GitError still accepts any String, so a future arm that formats something else into it reintroduces the exposure with nothing to stop it.

This is the shape .claude/rules/verification.md names: 'An invariant you can state is not an invariant the code enforces.' selfie-cvpm fixes the git side by construction; this is the adjacent hop that stays convention-only.

Fix direction: give SyncError::GitError the same redacting/bounded type selfie-cvpm introduces, so the guarantee survives the hop. Cheap once that type exists -- file now so it is not lost when cvpm closes.

Depends on selfie-cvpm landing first. Found by the selfie-cvpm plan reviewer.

title: MCP sync tools cannot be tested end to end because the service type is fixed
description:
crates/mcp-server/src/server.rs:39 fixes the concrete type:

  type ConcreteSyncService = SyncServiceImpl<GixGitAdapter, ConcreteDotfileService>;

So no test can inject a mock GitSyncProvider and assert on the actual JSON that selfie_sync_push / selfie_sync_pull / selfie_sync_status return. Tests can only reach one layer short of the real boundary -- they assert on the string event_collector.rs:34 serializes, not on the tool result an AI assistant actually receives.

This matters for the sync path specifically because that path has TWO distinct AI-facing exits with different shapes:
  1. the event stream -> event_collector.rs:33-35 -> {"status":"failure","error":...}
  2. server.rs:757-765 -> {"status":"error","message":...}  (bypasses the event stream entirely)
A test that covers only the first proves nothing about the second, and nothing today covers either at the tool boundary.

Fix direction: make the sync tool handlers generic over the service trait the way the package tools are, so a mock can be injected -- or add a seam that lets a test drive the tool handler with a substituted service. Compare how the package tools are structured; the boundary rule in .claude/rules/architecture.md says both adapters should consume the same trait.

Found by the selfie-cvpm plan author (U4 of the command-execution batch) while mapping every egress from git output to an AI transcript.

title: A streaming read failure names neither the command nor the directory
description:
crates/selfie/src/commands/shell.rs:485-490. handle_chunked_read_result_streaming builds its failure as:

  CommandError::IoError {
      command: "streaming command".to_string(),
      working_directory: std::env::current_dir().unwrap_or_else(...),
      ...
  }

Two defects in one constructor. The command field is a hardcoded literal rather than the command that actually failed. And working_directory re-reads the process's current directory instead of the recorded working_directory -- which is precisely the substitution execute_in_dir exists to avoid, since run_buffered:127-132 deliberately reports 'the directory the command actually ran in, not selfie's own, so a failure names the place the user configured.'

Consequence: a read failure during 'selfie package install' produces a diagnostic that identifies neither what ran nor where. Diagnostics only -- no incorrect behavior and no egress -- but it defeats the context the surrounding code goes out of its way to preserve.

Found by the selfie-ql8m plan author and confirmed by its reviewer (U1 of the command-execution batch); verified by the lead.

title: execute_streaming's exit_status.unwrap() is guarded only by a comment
description:
crates/selfie/src/commands/shell.rs:437: status: exit_status.unwrap(), guarded by a // SAFETY: comment asserting that the loop only exits when process_done is true, which is only set after exit_status is assigned Some(status).

The invariant is real today. Nothing enforces it. This is the exact shape .claude/rules/verification.md names: 'An invariant you can state is not an invariant the code enforces... If it matters, make it a type, a guard in a shared module, or a compile error.' A future break added to that loop for any reason turns this into a panic in the library -- and the selfie library panicking takes down whichever adapter is hosting it, CLI or MCP server.

Fix direction: restructure so the status cannot be absent by construction -- e.g. have the loop return the status rather than assign into an Option the code later unwraps, so the type carries the invariant instead of the comment.

Found by the selfie-ql8m plan reviewer (U1 of the command-execution batch); verified by the lead.
notes: LIKELY SUBSUMED by selfie-6bav (2026-07-30). This unwrap exists only because execute_streaming's hand-rolled loop needs a process_done/exit_status state machine. A FramedRead/Stream rewrite has no such Option to unwrap, so the invariant disappears rather than being enforced. Verify it is actually gone before closing.
close_reason: Closed

title: BoundedText's lossy decode defeats the byte-rendering leak scan
description:
Blocked on PR #78 (selfie-iuhz) landing; not a change to that PR.

selfie-gwhw taught the leak scan to look for a credential in BOTH renderings: as text, and as a Debug of Vec<u8> ([115, 51, 99, ...]). That closed the blind spot where std::process::Output's Debug switches to a byte array for non-UTF-8 content.

BoundedText::bound() decodes with String::from_utf8_lossy. Every invalid byte becomes U+FFFD. So on the stderr path, binary content reaching an event renders as replacement characters that match NEITHER needle:
  - the byte needle never matches, because the value is no longer bytes
  - the text needle matches only if the secret's readable prefix survives normalization at 12 characters

The two changes are individually correct and jointly reopen a narrow hole on one path. gwhw's scan assumes binary content stays binary; BoundedText makes it lossy text first.

Scope is narrow — it needs a secret that is BOTH non-UTF-8 AND has a short readable prefix, on the stderr path specifically. Overlaps selfie-i8qh (the same lossy blind spot, described generally); this bead is the concrete instance created by BoundedText. Consider closing them together.

Possible fix: a third needle derived from the lossy decoding of the secret, so whatever from_utf8_lossy would produce is also scanned for.

Found by selfie-gwhw's independent final reviewer, looking forward at #78 rather than at the code in front of it.
acceptance_criteria: A non-UTF-8 credential reaching stderr is caught by the leak scan in its lossily-decoded form.

title: resolve.rs copies the whole provider output a second time
description:
resolve.rs:268 calls output.stdout().to_vec() while 'output' is still live, so the provider's entire stdout exists twice at peak — roughly 2x for a dotfile whose content comes from a command.

The size cap is 8 MiB, so worst case is ~16 MiB transient rather than anything unbounded. Not urgent. But this is the credential-bearing path (command-sourced dotfile content), and a second copy is a second buffer that has to be reasoned about for zeroization if this project ever goes there.

Fix is likely to consume 'output' rather than borrow-then-copy. Check whether CommandOutput exposes an owning accessor; if not, adding one is the change.

Found by selfie-3hap's author while reading the surrounding code. Note selfie-ql8m also concerns resolve.rs:268 — that one is about TRUNCATED output being written past the cap, which is the more serious defect at the same line. Fix ql8m first; this may fall out of it.
acceptance_criteria: Provider output is not duplicated at peak.
close_reason: Closed

title: secrets.md does not load for the files that implement its leak-scanning rule
description:
.claude/rules/secrets.md's paths: frontmatter matches none of the files that implement the leak-scanning rule the file prescribes.

Not matched:
  crates/test-common/src/secrets.rs   the scanner itself (assert_secret_free)
  crates/selfie/tests/**              every leak-regression test that calls it

Matched today: crates/selfie/src/** (parts), three CLI files, crates/mcp-server/src/**.

So a session editing the scanner — or writing a new leak test — does not get the rule that governs it auto-loaded. That is the population most likely to weaken the scan by accident, and the least likely to have the rule in context.

This is not hypothetical for this file specifically: selfie-gwhw exists because the rule said 'scan for the secret literal', an instruction that was wrong once Vec<u8> Debug entered the picture, and nobody editing the tests had the rule in front of them to notice.

Scored 75 by selfie-gwhw's own code review — below its 80 fix-threshold, so deliberately left. Cheap to fix: add the two paths. Worth a moment's thought about whether crates/selfie/tests/** is too broad, since it would load the secrets rule for every integration test in the crate.

Note selfie-gwhw and selfie-iuhz both edit this file's frontmatter for other reasons; whoever takes this should land after both.
acceptance_criteria: Editing the leak scanner or a leak-regression test loads .claude/rules/secrets.md.
notes:
COORDINATION NOTE (2026-07-30): there are now THREE in-flight changes to .claude/rules/secrets.md's paths: frontmatter, not two.

This bead's description already gates it on selfie-gwhw and selfie-iuhz. Add a third: selfie-cvpm (U4 of the command-execution batch) adds crates/selfie/src/git/**/*.rs and crates/selfie/src/sync_service/**/*.rs -- confirmed by its plan reviewer to be genuinely unmatched by the current paths: list, so the addition is correct rather than cargo-culted.

No glob conflict between them: gwhw/iuhz add crates/test-common/src/secrets.rs and crates/selfie/tests/**, cvpm adds git/** and sync_service/**. But they edit the same frontmatter block, so expect a textual merge conflict and land this one last.

title: Nothing scans stdout or stderr for leaked secrets
description:
selfie's leak-regression tests cover two egress channels: the PackageEvent stream and the tracing subscriber. Direct writes to the process's stdout and stderr are scanned by nothing.

A stray println!, eprintln!, or dbg! on the resolve path would print a credential and fail no test in the repo. dbg! is the likeliest — it is a debugging reflex, it goes to stderr, and it uses {:?}, which on ResolvedContent prints '<N bytes>' but on a raw &[u8] or a String prints the content.

The library is not supposed to write to stdout/stderr at all (.claude/rules/architecture.md), so a lint may fit better than a test: deny println!/eprintln!/dbg! in crates/selfie/src outside #[cfg(test)]. That enforces the existing boundary rule and closes this as a side effect. clippy has print_stdout, print_stderr and dbg_macro lints, all allow-by-default.

Decide whether this is a gap to close or a documented boundary of what the leak tests cover — .claude/rules/secrets.md currently implies the event stream and tracing are the whole net.

Found while implementing selfie-gwhw.
acceptance_criteria: Either direct stdout/stderr writes from the library are prevented, or the leak tests' coverage boundary is documented.

title: No leak test exercises a non-UTF-8 credential end to end
description:
selfie-gwhw unit-tests the leak helper against non-UTF-8 secrets, but no integration fixture drives one through a real apply. Every end-to-end leak test uses an ASCII secret.

That matters because non-UTF-8 is the case where the byte rendering is the ONLY rendering: std::process::Output's Debug prints stdout as text when valid UTF-8 and as a byte array otherwise, so an ASCII credential and a binary one take different paths through the same code. The path that only binary content reaches has no end-to-end coverage.

selfie supports binary dotfile content deliberately — resolve.rs tests provider_output_is_byte_exact_including_non_utf8 (b"\x00\xff\xfe\x0a") and a_non_utf8_binding_survives_into_the_rendered_output (b"k: \xff\xfe").

Fix: one integration fixture in crates/selfie/tests/dotfile_service_tests.rs using a non-UTF-8 provider secret, asserting no leak, with a positive control proving the run produced it. Note selfie-i8qh first — a from_utf8_lossy rendering would escape the scan, so the fixture should be written after that is settled or it may pass for the wrong reason.

Found while implementing selfie-gwhw.
acceptance_criteria: An end-to-end leak test drives a non-UTF-8 credential through apply, with a working positive control.

title: from_utf8_lossy of a non-UTF-8 credential matches neither leak-scan needle
description:
selfie-gwhw's assert_secret_free scans two renderings: the secret as text, and its Debug-of-bytes form. A third rendering escapes both.

String::from_utf8_lossy of non-UTF-8 content replaces each invalid byte with U+FFFD. The result is neither the original text (the bytes are gone) nor the byte-array Debug (it is a string). A leak that formats a binary credential that way matches no needle.

This is the case selfie-gwhw leads with as its urgency argument: std::process::Output's Debug switches to a byte array for non-UTF-8 stdout, and selfie explicitly supports binary dotfile content (resolve.rs tests b"\x00\xff\xfe" and b"k: \xff\xfe"). So the scenario that motivated making the scan byte-aware is the one the byte-awareness does not cover — documented in the helper's limitations list rather than closed.

Closing it means a third needle: the lossy-decoded form of the secret, derived inside the helper alongside the other two so the choice is not re-made per call site.

Worth weighing first: how reachable is it? A leak would have to route binary content through from_utf8_lossy specifically, rather than Display or Debug. resolve.rs:265 does exactly that on the error branch, so it is not hypothetical.

Found while implementing selfie-gwhw.
acceptance_criteria: A leak of a non-UTF-8 secret rendered through from_utf8_lossy fails the leak-regression tests.
notes:
THE ORIGINAL DESCRIPTION IS WRONG AND OVERSTATES THE HOLE. Retracted by the selfie-gwhw author after its own code review scored this as the round's highest-confidence finding (100/100), and reproduced by probe.

'Matches neither needle' is false. A binary secret with a long readable prefix IS caught, as text — the module's own test demonstrates it.

ACCURATE PROPERTY: a lossy rendering is uncovered by the BYTE needle always, and by the TEXT needle only when the secret's readable prefix does not survive normalization at 12 characters. Where the prefix does survive, the lossy rendering is normally caught.

Two edges narrow it further, both found by probe rather than reasoning:
  - The gate is the SQUEEZED length, not the valid-UTF-8 prefix length. b"a b c d e f g " + [0xff,0xfe,0x00] has valid_up_to = 14, above the 12-character window, and still escapes both needles.
  - squeeze also deletes literal backslash-n / backslash-r / backslash-t PAIRS, so a 13-non-whitespace-character prefix can still produce no needle.

The hole is real but narrower than filed, and selfie-gwhw now documents it and pins BOTH sides with tests — including a_lossy_rendering_escapes_a_whitespace_heavy_readable_prefix, which asserts the escaping case rather than claiming coverage. So this is no longer an undocumented gap; it is a documented, tested boundary.

Downgraded P2 to P3 accordingly. Closing it means a third needle for the lossy-decoded form; weigh that against the fact that the escape now requires a whitespace-heavy readable prefix specifically.

title: Leak tests have no byte-aware positive control (assert_secret_present)
description:
selfie-gwhw makes the NEGATIVE leak assertion byte-aware: assert_secret_free scans for both the text rendering and the Debug-of-bytes rendering of a secret. The POSITIVE controls beside it were left literal-only, deliberately, because converting them would silently invert their meaning.

Two sites:
  crates/selfie/tests/command_output_egress_tests.rs:84   assert ... contains(SECRET)
  crates/selfie/tests/dotfile_service_tests.rs:2656

These are the assertions that prove a leak test is not passing vacuously — that the run genuinely produced the secret through its acknowledged channel. They scan for the literal only. If an acknowledged channel ever renders the secret as bytes rather than text, the control silently stops observing anything and the negative assertion beside it becomes unfalsifiable — which is the exact failure .claude/rules/testing.md warns about, arriving through the control rather than the test.

Fix: an assert_secret_present in crates/test-common/src/secrets.rs sharing anchor() with assert_secret_free, so both directions use the same needles.

Found while implementing selfie-gwhw; excluded there because converting the call sites without the new helper would have inverted them.
acceptance_criteria: Positive controls in leak tests are byte-aware, using the same needles as the negative assertion.

title: CommandError::NonZeroExit is never constructed in production
description:
ShellCommandRunner never returns CommandError::NonZeroExit. run_buffered and execute_streaming both return Ok(CommandOutput) regardless of exit status — a non-zero exit is reported through CommandOutput::is_success, which crates/selfie/src/commands/runner.rs:133 documents explicitly as the intended contract.

Every occurrence at HEAD:
  runner.rs:287             the variant definition
  event.rs:1270             a match arm (consumption, not construction)
  resolve.rs:252            prose in a doc comment
  commands.rs:83, 99, 114   constructions, all inside #[cfg(test)] mod tests
  cli/src/event_processor.rs:714   construction, inside a test
Zero production constructions.

Why this is NOT a simple delete, and why selfie-3hap's unit deliberately did not do it:
  - event.rs:1270 matches it and maps to CommandFailure::ExecutionFailed, which is where the stderr bound lives. Removing the variant removes that arm.
  - .claude/rules/secrets.md builds standing guidance around this variant specifically: its Debug carries stdout while its Display does not, which is the basis for the file's 'use to_string(), never {:?}' rule. Deleting it without rewriting that guidance would leave the rule pointing at nothing.
  - Tests exercise it as a fixture for the failure path.

So the question is not 'delete the dead variant' but 'what should represent a non-zero exit in the error type, given the runner deliberately does not treat it as an error'. Options: keep it as the vocabulary a caller uses when it decides a non-zero exit IS an error (in which case document that, since today it reads as something the runner returns); or remove it and rework the event.rs arm and secrets.md together.

Found while planning selfie-3hap, which fixes the DOCUMENTATION half — three # Errors blocks claiming these methods return it — but leaves the variant alone.
acceptance_criteria: Either the variant has a stated purpose that matches how it is used, or it is removed along with the event mapping and the secrets.md guidance built on it.
notes:
CORRECTION to the description's site list, caught by the selfie-3hap author and verified against the tree.

There are TWO construction sites, not five, and both are tests:
  crates/selfie/src/commands.rs:83                 construction (let error = CommandError::NonZeroExit {)
  crates/cli/src/event_processor.rs:714            construction
The other two the description cites are not constructions:
  commands.rs:99   a match PATTERN in the same test
  commands.rs:114  the string literal inside '_ => panic!("Expected NonZeroExit error")'

This strengthens the substantive claim rather than weakening it: the variant is not a lightly-used one, it is one with two test fixtures and no production use at all.

Also worth recording for whoever takes this: the disclaimer at runner.rs:133-134 reads 'A non-zero exit is not an error: it is reported through CommandOutput::is_success, AS WITH THE OTHER EXECUTION METHODS.' So the correct contract was documented and explicitly asserted to generalize, while three sibling methods' # Errors blocks contradicted it. selfie-3hap's unit lifts that disclaimer to the trait doc, which is what the clause was already claiming.
close_reason: Closed

title: ExecutionFailed.stderr is bounded by convention, not by construction
description:
selfie-ppp removes stdout from CommandFailure::ExecutionFailed entirely, which is STRUCTURAL — there is no field, so the leak cannot be written. The stderr bound is not: CommandFailure is a public enum, so ExecutionFailed's fields are public and any struct-variant literal can set stderr unbounded. crates/cli/src/event_processor.rs:674 does exactly that in a test.

The guarantee holds today only because the two library constructors (From<CommandError> at event.rs:1275 and command_failed at event.rs:1717) are the only production writers, and both call truncate_stderr. ErrorDetail.stderr's new doc comment says 'Already truncated by the library' — true, and true only by that convention.

This is .claude/rules/verification.md's case verbatim: 'An invariant you can state is not an invariant the code enforces. If it matters, make it a type, a guard in a shared module, or a compile error.'

Fix direction: make the field private with a constructor that truncates, so a literal cannot bypass it. Note that changing the enum's shape has adapter impact — event_processor.rs destructures it — so this is not a one-liner.

Related: selfie-iuhz (the same bound is mandated by a rule that one site already violates and two crates cannot call).

Found by the final reviewer on selfie-ppp, which deliberately did not widen scope to fix it.
acceptance_criteria: A struct-variant literal cannot put unbounded stderr into ExecutionFailed.
close_reason: Closed

title: CommandError::Callback is a dead variant whose Display writes its payload verbatim
description:
crates/selfie/src/commands/runner.rs:313 defines CommandError::Callback(OutputChunk). 'grep -rn Callback crates/' returns exactly one hit — the definition. Nothing constructs it.

Its Display (runner.rs:34-40) writes the chunk's inner string verbatim. If it were ever constructed, From<CommandError>'s catch-all arm ('_ => OperationFailure::Generic(err.to_string())', event.rs:1284) would carry that string into PackageEvent::Completed and thence to both the CLI display and the MCP JSON.

This is the one place where .claude/rules/secrets.md's guidance — 'use to_string(), never {:?}' — would NOT be sufficient, because the leak is in Display rather than Debug. Every other CommandError variant's #[error(...)] omits stdout, which is what makes that rule safe elsewhere.

Unreachable today, so not a live exposure. But it is a loaded gun in a match arm designed to be a safe fallback. Either delete the variant, or bound its Display, before streaming ever grows an error path that constructs it.

Found by the final reviewer on selfie-ppp.
acceptance_criteria: CommandError::Callback is removed, or its Display cannot emit unbounded command output.
close_reason: Closed

title: CheckResult carries a check command's stdout and the CLI prints it
description:
CheckResult::Failed and CheckResult::Success carry the check command's stdout, and the CLI prints it at crates/cli/src/commands/package/check.rs:139-149 and :190-210. MCP is unaffected — it renders a label only.

Same class as selfie-ppp (a user-defined command's output reaching a display verbatim) but a different type and a different display path, so selfie-ppp's fix to CommandFailure::ExecutionFailed does not cover it. Notably this one is NOT gated on the multi-error summary's two-error threshold, so it surfaces on a single failing check.

Found while tracing every exit for selfie-ppp; held out of that unit's scope deliberately.

When fixing, apply the same policy selfie-ppp establishes rather than inventing a second one: a user-defined command's stdout is content selfie does not control and may be a credential; stderr may be forwarded truncated on failure.
acceptance_criteria: A check command's stdout is not surfaced verbatim by default, consistent with whatever policy selfie-ppp establishes.
notes:
FRAMING CORRECTED by the selfie-iuhz plan reviewer. My earlier note said the event-stream exposure was the concern and that MCP does not serialize it. The first half needs narrowing:

CheckResult::Success/Failed do carry the check command's whole stdout AND stderr unbounded into PackageEvent::CheckResultCompleted (check.rs:261-263, :270-273). But this is NOT an unintended-egress bug. Verified: check_status_label (mcp-server/src/event_collector.rs:299-307) maps CheckResult to a static label only, and nothing serializes stdout outside test fixtures — so it never reaches the assistant-facing JSON. docs/package-files.md:358-360 documents terminal display as deliberate, and crates/selfie/tests/command_output_egress_tests.rs:8-17 explicitly carves it out of the failure-value invariant.

THE ACTUAL RESIDUAL IS UNBOUNDED SIZE, NOT UNINTENDED EGRESS. A check command producing megabytes of output puts all of it in an event payload and prints all of it to the terminal, with no bound anywhere — while the failure path beside it is bounded to 2000 bytes. That asymmetry is the thing to resolve, and it is a smaller and more tractable question than 'should check output be shown at all', which the docs already answer yes.

Anyone taking this: do not write it up as a leak. It is a missing bound on a deliberately-displayed channel.

title: Decide whether test-lib belongs in just check and the CLAUDE.md checklist
description:
PR #70 added a CI step running 'cargo test -p selfie' alone, because every workspace-wide command unifies the with_mocks feature in from another crate's dev-dependencies and so cannot catch the library losing access to it.

That gate now exists in three places with three different answers:
- .github/workflows/ci.yml runs it as its own step. Yes.
- Justfile has it as 'test-lib' but 'just check' does NOT include it.
- CLAUDE.md's pre-commit checklist is four steps and does not mention it.

selfie-blkr makes the pre-commit-check skill run 'just check' AND 'just test-lib', which closes the gap for agents using the skill but makes the skill a SUPERSET of the documented checklist — a human running 'just check' or following CLAUDE.md still misses it. That is a smaller, deliberately-created drift, flagged rather than hidden by the author of that fix.

Decide the single answer: either add test-lib to 'just check' and make CLAUDE.md's checklist five steps (so every path covers it), or record that it is CI's job alone and remove it from the skill. The current three-way split is what produced selfie-blkr in the first place.

Note the cost side: 'just check' already runs the workspace suite, so adding test-lib means one extra compile of selfie at a different feature set. Measured on this machine it is a few seconds warm.
acceptance_criteria: cargo test -p selfie is either in every local gate path or explicitly documented as CI-only, not present in some and absent from others.
notes:
ANSWER REVISED 2026-07-29 by the maintainer, superseding the earlier 'add it to the checklist' decision.

The question was wrong-shaped. 'Where should test-lib live?' assumes a hand-picked crate+feature combination is the right instrument. It is not. Verified: selfie is the ONLY crate in the workspace with an optional feature (with_mocks = ["mockall"]; mockall is the only optional=true dependency anywhere), and selfie-cli / selfie-mcp / test-common have no [features] section at all. So isolating any other crate would catch nothing, and isolating selfie covers exactly one combination.

RESOLUTION: cargo-hack in CI, replacing the ad-hoc 'Test the library crate alone' step PR #70 added:
    cargo hack --each-feature test -p selfie
and REMOVE test-lib from CLAUDE.md's pre-commit checklist entirely. The break this guards against (test-common dropping its features request) can only reach main through a PR, and CI gates PRs — a pre-commit step is the wrong layer.

Why this is better than what it replaces: it covers every feature combination rather than the single one the workspace run happens to produce, and it generalizes. Add a second optional feature later and cargo-hack covers the combinations automatically, whereas a hand-picked test-lib step would silently under-test and nobody would notice.

Being implemented in the selfie-blkr PR; close against that.
close_reason:
Fixed in PR #73 (merged d9bb7f9).

selfie-blkr: the pre-commit-check skill was DELETED rather than corrected. It duplicated a checklist CLAUDE.md already carries and already loads every session, and that duplication is what let the two drift apart. CLAUDE.md's checklist now delegates to 'just check', so no second copy of the commands exists to weaken. Premise verified empirically rather than restated: on an isolated copy with a planted clippy::needless_return, 'cargo clippy --all-targets' exits 0 while printing the warning and '-- -D warnings' exits 101 on identical code.

selfie-it6l: resolved differently than the bead framed it. The question assumed a hand-picked crate+feature invocation was the right instrument. selfie is the only crate in the workspace with an optional feature (with_mocks; mockall is the only optional=true dependency), so it was the only crate worth isolating and nothing said why. CI now runs 'cargo hack --each-feature test -p selfie', covering all four combinations instead of the one the workspace run produces, and extending itself if a second feature appears. Removed from the local checklist: the break can only reach main through a PR, and CI gates PRs. Verified the replacement is a strict superset — deleting test-common's features line fails cargo-hack on pass 2 of 4 with the predicted from_parts error, and the old gate exits 101 on the same mutation.

selfie-cm1h: the trailing sentence was retensed and its citation historicized rather than deleted, so it still explains why obsolete '--features with_mocks' instructions exist elsewhere. Worth recording why this was more than a P4 nit: THREE independent agents misread that sentence during this batch — one reported CLAUDE.md as stale, one claimed 'just test-lib' would fail every time and cited it as proof, one filed it as a stale-docs finding on an unrelated PR. All three were wrong. The mechanism, diagnosed by the selfie-ppp author, is that all three misread a TRAILING CLAUSE qualifying an earlier claim; a reader who stops at the first assertion gets the opposite meaning. The fix leads with 'The command compiles today.' as a standalone sentence.

title: The typos pre-commit hook may not affect the commit it fires on
description:
A PreToolUse hook in .claude/settings.json runs 'typos --write-changes' before any 'git commit'. It EDITS FILES ON DISK, which means whether the fix reaches the commit depends on how the commit is made:

- Agent stages first, then runs a plain 'git commit': the commit takes the INDEX, which was built before the hook rewrote the working tree. The typo fix stays unstaged and CI's check-typos job still fails — the hook did work, silently, for nothing.
- Agent runs 'git commit -- <paths>': the paths are re-read from the working tree at commit time, so the fix lands.

So the hook is effective on one commit path and silently ineffective on the other. .claude/rules/verification.md recommends 'git commit -- <paths>' (for unrelated staging-safety reasons), which happens to be the path where the hook works — so the failure may be masked in practice by a convention adopted for a different purpose. That is a fragile reason for a hook to function.

Stated as a mechanism by the author of selfie-blkr from reading the hook, NOT as a tested observation. Confirm it before fixing: stage a file containing a typo, run a plain 'git commit', and check whether the committed blob carries the fix.

If confirmed, options: have the hook re-stage what it changed ('git add -u' on the affected paths), or make it a check that BLOCKS the commit rather than a silent rewrite, so the agent is told rather than having its commit quietly diverge from its working tree.
acceptance_criteria: The typos hook either affects every commit path it fires on, or blocks the commit so the discrepancy cannot be silent.
notes:
FRAMING SHARPENED by the final reviewer on selfie-blkr. The mechanism as filed is correct, but the finding is worse than 'the hook sometimes does nothing':

.claude/rules/verification.md PRESCRIBES 'git commit -- <paths>' as the preferred commit form (for unrelated staging-safety reasons). That is precisely the form under which the hook's rewrite DOES reach the commit — meaning the repo's own recommended convention is the one that commits hook-edited content the author never reviewed or staged. The plain-git-commit path, where the fix is silently dropped, is the one the convention steers people away from.

So both branches are wrong in opposite directions: the discouraged path silently discards the fix, and the recommended path silently includes an unreviewed edit. Neither tells the author anything. That argues for making the hook BLOCK with a message rather than rewrite, since the failure is silence in both directions rather than a missing re-stage.

title: A live plan doc prescribes the bare clippy form as its per-step gate
description:
docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-24-provider-sourced-dotfiles.md prescribes 'cargo clippy --all-targets' with no '-- -D warnings' at roughly ten places (:25, :202, :387, :564, :741, :1041, :1182, :1240, :1307, :1317), and :25 labels it '(zero warnings)' — the exact mislabel selfie-blkr fixes in the pre-commit-check skill.

This one matters more than the others because it is LIVE: the plan is dated 2026-07-24, it covers provider-sourced dotfiles, and agents have been working in that area since. An agent executing the plan step by step runs the under-reporting gate at every checkpoint and can ship a warning to a red CI while believing each step passed.

Older documents carry the same text but are archival records of completed work rather than instructions anyone will follow: docs/superpowers/plans/2026-03-15-streaming-package-list.md:346,375; docs/superpowers/plans/2026-03-20-config-file-deployment.md (about 12 occurrences); and three specs. Fixing the live plan is the point; the archival ones are a low-priority sweep and arguably should be left as the historical record of what was actually run.

Note these files are local-excluded working artifacts per project convention, so 'fixing' them may mean fixing the template or habit that produces them rather than the files themselves.

Found by the author of selfie-blkr.
acceptance_criteria: The live plan doc prescribes the CI clippy form, or plan docs stop prescribing gate commands inline.
notes: UNDERCOUNTED at filing. The final reviewer on selfie-blkr found docs/superpowers/plans/2026-03-20-config-file-deployment.md carries 14 MORE bare 'cargo clippy --all-targets' occurrences (lines 275, 370, 471, 692, 765, 924, 1010, 1137, 1168, 1224, 1265, 1368, 1425 and following), on top of the ten in the 2026-07-24 provider-sourced-dotfiles plan. Also: BOTH line 25 and line 1317 of the 07-24 plan mislabel it '(zero warnings)', not just line 25.

title: TILT.md documents 14 just targets that do not exist
description:
TILT.md (last touched 2026-03-16) references 17 'just' invocations. 'just --list' shows the Justfile provides only: build, check, clippy, default, docs, fmt, fmt-check, outdated, test, test-cli, test-lib.

Of TILT.md's references, only 'just build', 'just docs' and 'just fmt' exist. These do not:
  just docker build-images / clean / logs / rebuild-images / shell-alpine / shell-debian / start / status / stop
  just local-clippy
  just local-test
  just tilt test / test-alpine / test-debian

Anyone following TILT.md gets 'error: Justfile does not contain recipe' on nearly every command in it. There is exactly one Justfile in the repo (confirmed by find; no submodule Justfiles), so this is not a path problem.

Two notes. First, 'just local-clippy' is additionally the weaker-gate flavor of selfie-blkr — whatever it once ran, a name like that suggests a local variant of the clippy gate, which is the pattern that under-reports. Second, the doc looks broadly stale rather than wrong in one line, so the fix is probably to rewrite or delete it rather than patch names; decide whether the Tilt/Docker workflow it describes still exists at all before restoring any of it.

Found by the author of selfie-blkr while checking whether the same defect appeared elsewhere.
acceptance_criteria: TILT.md describes commands that exist, or is removed if the workflow it documents no longer does.

title: track-dotfile strands the copied source file when the package save fails
description:
crates/selfie/src/dotfile_service/service.rs:1607 copies the user's dotfile into the package directory, then :1619 calls save_package. If the save fails, the copied file is left behind with no cleanup.

Measured on the selfie-6lz4 branch, where the new save guard makes this reachable: 'selfie package track-dotfile' on a package carrying an unrecognized key refuses the save, leaves '.newfile' in packages/<name>/, and a retry after fixing the typo then fails with 'Source file already exists at .../creds/.newfile. Remove it first or choose a different file.' The user must manually delete a file they never knowingly created.

Pre-existing ordering — ANY save_package failure (permissions, disk full, serialization error) does this. selfie-6lz4 amplifies it by adding a new and quite reachable failure mode rather than creating it.

Fix: copy after a successful save, or remove the copied file on the save-failure path. The first is better if nothing in the save depends on the file already being present — check that before choosing.

Found by the final reviewer on selfie-6lz4.
acceptance_criteria: A failed package save during track-dotfile leaves no copied source file behind.

title: The non-unix arms of write_file_no_follow and write_file_private are built by no CI job
description:
crates/selfie/src/fs/real.rs:141-155 is the #[cfg(not(unix))] arm of write_file_no_follow — a racy symlink_metadata fallback, including deliberate handling for 'a stat that fails for any reason other than absent is an error'. Every job in .github/workflows/ci.yml runs on ubuntu-latest, so that branch has never been compiled, let alone run, anywhere. The same is true of the Windows arm of write_file_private.

The comments on those branches are careful and appear correct. They are simply unverified: a syntax error, a type error, or an inverted condition would not be caught by anything. Code that cannot fail a build is code nobody has checked.

This is a standing repo-wide gap rather than something selfie-4m9 introduced — noting it there only because that change added a second such branch on a security-relevant write path, where an untested fallback is worse than elsewhere.

Options: add a windows-latest (and/or macos-latest) job to CI so the arms at least compile; or, if non-unix is not actually supported, say so and make the arms a compile_error! rather than a plausible-looking implementation that has never run. The second is cheaper and more honest if nobody is running selfie on Windows.

Found by the final reviewer on selfie-4m9.
acceptance_criteria: Every platform arm of the filesystem writers is either compiled by CI or replaced with an explicit refusal to support that platform.

title: save_package shells out to dprint from inside the selfie library
description:
crates/selfie/src/package/repository/yaml.rs:250-270: YamlPackageRepository::save_package spawns 'dprint fmt' on the file it just wrote, with a 5-second poll-and-kill loop.

Two problems.

First, it is a boundary violation in spirit. The selfie library is supposed to be frontend-agnostic — CLAUDE.md says it should not assume it is called from a CLI, and .claude/rules/architecture.md routes all outward effects through the event system. Shelling out to a developer-machine code formatter is an undeclared dependency on the caller's PATH and on a tool that has nothing to do with the domain. An MCP server, a GUI, or a test harness on a machine without dprint gets different behavior with no signal (it is silently skipped).

Second, the poll-and-kill loop is a hand-rolled timeout in a library that already has a CommandRunner port with timeout handling. If formatting saved files is genuinely desired, it belongs in the adapter that knows a developer is present, or behind the existing port.

Pre-existing; found by the final reviewer on selfie-6lz4 while tracing save_package for an unrelated fail-open.
acceptance_criteria: Saved package formatting either moves out of the library or goes through an existing port, rather than the library spawning dprint directly.

title: Decide and record whether the two dotfile writers should keep diverging on symlinks
description:
After selfie-4m9 selfie has two write paths that treat a symlinked target OPPOSITELY:

- Repository-file dotfiles: REFUSE (O_NOFOLLOW), warn, skip. Rationale: the user's symlink is legitimate config, the content is recoverable, and destroying the link on a routine unprompted update was measured to be the default path, not an edge case.
- Secret/provider-sourced dotfiles: REPLACE the link atomically. Rationale: a credential must never reach an attacker-chosen destination, and replacement is the only safe way to COMPLETE the write.

Both are correct in isolation and each is documented on its own side. But the divergence is currently an emergent consequence of two separately-reasoned decisions, not a recorded one, and nothing states that they SHOULD differ. The next person to notice will read it as an inconsistency and 'fix' it — in whichever direction they happen to be standing.
